topics.title: Conflicts of Interest & Prohibited Practices
topics.reading:
Lending to and borrowing from clients

NASAA treats most loans between a financial professional and a client as unethical, because the client's trust can be exploited. Under the NASAA statements of policy:

  • An adviser or IAR may borrow money or securities from a client only if the client is a financial institution in the business of lending, such as a bank. The IA policy also allows borrowing from a client that is a broker-dealer or an affiliate of the adviser.
  • An adviser may lend to a client only if the adviser itself is a financial institution in the business of lending, or the client is an affiliate of the adviser.
  • Agents are likewise barred from borrowing from or lending to customers, apart from these lending-institution situations and whatever the employing broker-dealer permits under its written procedures.

A loan from a wealthy client who happens to be a friend, or from an elderly client who "insists," is prohibited.

Sharing in a customer's account

An agent may share in a customer account's profits or losses only if:

  1. it is a joint account;
  2. the agent has written authorization from both the customer and the broker-dealer;
  3. the agent shares in direct proportion to their own financial contribution to the account.

Under FINRA Rule 2150, accounts of the agent's immediate family are exempt from the proportionality requirement.

Guarantees

Guaranteeing a client against loss, or promising a particular result, is prohibited. Offering to "make up the difference" or to buy the position back at the purchase price are both guarantees. Accurately describing a security that a third party guarantees, such as a Treasury backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. government or an insured municipal bond, is not a guarantee by the agent.

Selling away

Selling away means effecting securities transactions that are not recorded on the broker-dealer's books, for example selling a private placement to clients on the side. It is unethical unless the broker-dealer authorizes it in writing before the transaction is executed.

Trading abuses

PracticeWhat it is
ChurningExcessive trading for commissions relative to the account's size, objectives and character
Front runningTrading for your own or the firm's account ahead of a customer's block order you know about, to profit from the price move it will cause
Scalping (IA)Buying a security, recommending it to clients or the public, then selling into the price rise
Unauthorized tradingPlacing a trade in a non-discretionary account without the client's prior approval
Market manipulationWash trades, matched orders, marking the close, or spreading rumors to move prices
Commission splittingSharing commissions with anyone not registered as an agent of the same (or an affiliated) broker-dealer is unethical

Insider trading and MNPI

Trading while aware of material nonpublic information (MNPI) obtained in breach of a duty, or passing it to someone who trades, is illegal. Both the tipper and the tippee are liable, and a tipper can be liable even without trading personally. Key rules:

  • Advisers Act Section 204A requires every adviser to establish, maintain and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to prevent misuse of MNPI by the adviser and its associated persons. Broker-dealers have a similar duty under the Exchange Act. A common control is an information barrier (sometimes called a "Chinese wall") between research or investment banking and trading.
  • Under ITSFEA (1988), the SEC may seek a civil penalty of up to three times the profit gained or loss avoided. Controlling persons (firms and supervisors) who knew or recklessly ignored the risk and failed to take steps to prevent the violation face penalties up to the greater of $1 million (inflation-adjusted) or three times the profit gained or loss avoided.
  • Criminal penalties under the Exchange Act reach 20 years in prison and fines of up to $5 million for individuals and $25 million for firms. Traders who traded at the same time as the insider (contemporaneous traders) may sue.

Personal trading: the code of ethics

SEC Rule 204A-1 requires advisers to adopt a written code of ethics. Access persons must report:

  • their holdings within 10 days of becoming an access person and then annually;
  • their transactions quarterly, within 30 days after each quarter ends.

They also need the firm's pre-approval before buying IPOs or limited offerings (private placements).

Other conflicts to disclose or avoid

  • Referral fees and compensation for recommending products.
  • Being an officer or director of an issuer the firm recommends.
  • Recommending securities in which the firm is a market maker or underwriter.
  • Acting as a dual registrant, where a representative switches between advice and brokerage roles.

The fiduciary remedy for an adviser is to eliminate the conflict or fully and fairly disclose it so the client can give informed consent.

Trap: Sharing in a customer account needs written approval from both the customer and the broker-dealer. Written approval from the customer alone is not enough.
keyPoints: Borrowing from or lending to clients is prohibited unless the client (for borrowing) or the adviser (for lending) is a financial institution in the business of lending; limited affiliate or BD exceptions apply for IAs.
Sharing in profits or losses requires a joint account, written authorization from the customer and the BD, and sharing proportional to contribution (immediate family excepted).
Selling away (trades off the BD's books) is unethical unless the BD authorizes it in writing before execution.
Guaranteeing a client against loss is prohibited; describing a third-party guaranteed security accurately is allowed.
Front running is trading ahead of a known customer block order; scalping is buying, recommending, then selling into the rise.
Section 204A requires written procedures to prevent misuse of MNPI; tipper and tippee are both liable.
ITSFEA: civil penalty up to 3 times the profit gained or loss avoided; controlling persons up to the greater of $1M (adjusted) or 3 times.
Code of ethics: holdings reports within 10 days and annually, quarterly transaction reports within 30 days, and pre-approval for IPOs and private placements.

topics.title: Fiduciary Duty, Reg BI & NASAA Unethical Practices
topics.reading:
The adviser's fiduciary duty

Investment advisers are fiduciaries. The duty comes from the antifraud provision of Section 206 of the Advisers Act, as interpreted in SEC v. Capital Gains Research Bureau (1963), and applies under state law too. The SEC's 2019 interpretation describes two parts:

  • Duty of care. Give advice in the client's best interest, based on a reasonable understanding of the client's objectives, finances and risk tolerance. Seek best execution when the adviser chooses the broker. Monitor the account at a frequency that fits the agreed relationship.
  • Duty of loyalty. Never put the adviser's interests ahead of the client's. Make full and fair disclosure of all material facts about the relationship, including conflicts of interest. Eliminate conflicts, or disclose them well enough that the client can give informed consent.

Best execution means seeking the most favorable terms reasonably available. That takes into account price, commission, speed, reliability, the quality of execution and research, not simply the lowest commission.

Broker-dealers: Regulation Best Interest

Since June 30, 2020, broker-dealers and their agents have had to act in the best interest of a retail customer at the time a recommendation is made, without putting the firm's or agent's interests ahead of the customer's. A retail customer is a natural person who uses the recommendation mainly for personal, family or household purposes. Reg BI has four component obligations:

  1. Disclosure: the capacity, fees, scope of services and conflicts;
  2. Care: reasonable diligence, care and skill, and considering reasonably available alternatives and costs;
  3. Conflict of interest: written policies to identify, disclose, mitigate or eliminate conflicts;
  4. Compliance: written policies reasonably designed to achieve compliance.

Reg BI is not a fiduciary standard, and it generally does not require ongoing account monitoring unless the firm agrees to monitor. For non-retail customers, FINRA's suitability rule (Rule 2111) still applies. It has three parts: reasonable-basis (suitable for at least some investors), customer-specific (suitable for this customer) and quantitative (not excessive in total). Know your customer (FINRA 2090) requires reasonable diligence to learn the essential facts about every customer.

Form CRS (the client relationship summary) is a short plain-English document, at most 2 pages (4 for dual registrants), that broker-dealers and advisers give retail investors. An adviser delivers it before or at the time of entering into the advisory contract. A broker-dealer delivers it before or at the earliest of a recommendation, an order or opening an account.

NASAA unethical practices: investment advisers and IARs

NASAA's statement of policy lists conduct that is grounds for denial, suspension or revocation. The list includes:

  • recommending unsuitable investments;
  • exercising discretion without written authority within 10 business days;
  • excessive trading;
  • placing orders based on third-party instructions without written authority;
  • borrowing from or lending to clients, outside the exceptions;
  • misrepresenting qualifications, services or fees;
  • failing to disclose material conflicts;
  • charging an unreasonable fee;
  • guaranteeing results;
  • publishing misleading advertisements;
  • disclosing a client's identity or affairs without consent, unless required by law;
  • entering into a contract that is not in writing or that allows assignment without consent;
  • including a hedge clause;
  • failing to have written MNPI procedures;
  • providing a report or recommendation prepared by someone else without disclosing that fact.
Trap: The "someone else's report" rule does not apply when the adviser uses published research reports or statistical analyses as the basis for its advice, or orders such a report in the normal course of business. Passing off a custom report written by another firm as your own is unethical.

NASAA unethical practices: broker-dealers and agents

  • churning;
  • unsuitable recommendations;
  • unauthorized trades;
  • exercising discretion without prior written authority;
  • extending credit in violation of Regulation T;
  • failing to deliver securities or funds promptly;
  • charging unreasonable commissions, markups or markdowns;
  • market manipulation;
  • front running;
  • misrepresenting the status of an account;
  • failing to bring written customer complaints to the broker-dealer's attention;
  • selling away;
  • guaranteeing against loss;
  • sharing in accounts without written approval;
  • splitting commissions with unregistered persons.

Splitting a commission with another agent registered with the same broker-dealer is permitted.

Investment adviserBroker-dealer (retail)
StandardFiduciary (care and loyalty) for the whole relationshipReg BI: best interest at the time of the recommendation
MonitoringConsistent with the agreed relationshipNot required unless agreed
Main disclosureForm ADV Part 2 and Form CRSForm CRS and Reg BI disclosures
keyPoints: The IA fiduciary duty (Advisers Act Section 206, Capital Gains Research Bureau) has two parts: care and loyalty.
Duty of care: best-interest advice, best execution and appropriate monitoring. Duty of loyalty: full and fair disclosure of material facts and conflicts, and never putting the adviser first.
Best execution weighs price, commission, speed, reliability and research, not just the lowest commission.
Reg BI (June 30, 2020): BDs act in a retail customer's best interest at the time of the recommendation; four obligations are disclosure, care, conflict of interest and compliance.
Reg BI is not a fiduciary standard and does not generally require ongoing monitoring.
Form CRS: 2 pages maximum (4 for dual registrants); IAs deliver it before or at the time of entering the contract.
Passing off another person's report as your own is unethical; using published research is permitted.
BD and agent unethical practices include churning, unauthorized trades, selling away, and failing to forward customer complaints.

topics.title: Anti-Money Laundering (AML)
topics.reading:
The legal framework

The Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) of 1970, strengthened by Title III of the USA PATRIOT Act (2001), requires financial institutions, including broker-dealers, to detect and report money laundering and terrorist financing. FinCEN, part of the Treasury Department, administers the reporting rules. FINRA Rule 3310 requires every broker-dealer to have a written AML program, approved in writing by senior management, that includes:

  • policies and procedures to detect and report suspicious activity;
  • a designated AML compliance officer;
  • ongoing employee training;
  • independent testing, generally every year;
  • risk-based customer due diligence.

FinCEN adopted a rule in 2024 extending AML program and suspicious activity reporting duties to SEC-registered and exempt reporting advisers, but it has postponed the rule's effective date (to 2028). On the exam, AML duties are tested mostly in the broker-dealer context.

Three stages of money laundering

  1. Placement: getting illegal cash into the financial system, for example through deposits or buying money orders. This is the stage where criminals are most exposed.
  2. Layering: hiding where the money came from through a series of transactions, such as wires between accounts in different countries or buying and selling securities quickly.
  3. Integration: bringing the now clean-looking money back into the legitimate economy, for example by buying real estate or businesses.

Reporting requirements

ReportTriggerKey details
Currency Transaction Report (CTR)Cash (currency) transactions of more than $10,000 in one business day, including several cash transactions that add up to more than $10,000Filed with FinCEN within 15 calendar days; routine, not an accusation
Suspicious Activity Report (SAR)For broker-dealers, transactions of $5,000 or more that the firm knows, suspects or has reason to suspect involve illegal funds, are designed to evade BSA rules, have no apparent lawful purpose, or use the firm to facilitate crimeFiled within 30 calendar days of first detecting the facts; the customer must not be told; supporting records kept 5 years
Funds transfer recordsWires of $3,000 or moreRecordkeeping and the "travel rule"

Structuring means deliberately breaking cash transactions into smaller amounts to avoid a CTR, for example depositing $9,500 on several days in a row. It is a federal crime even if the money is legitimate. A request to avoid "paperwork" is a red flag that should lead the firm to consider filing a SAR. An agent who helps a customer structure also commits a crime.

Customer Identification Program (CIP)

Before opening an account, the firm must collect at least four items:

  • name;
  • date of birth, for an individual;
  • address: a residential or business street address for an individual, not just a P.O. box;
  • identification number: a taxpayer ID number for U.S. persons; for non-U.S. persons, a TIN, passport number, alien ID card number or other government-issued ID number.

The firm verifies identity within a reasonable time before or after opening the account, keeps CIP records, gives customers notice that their identity is being verified, and checks names against government lists. Under the customer due diligence (CDD) rule, the firm must also identify the beneficial owners of legal-entity customers: each person who owns 25% or more, plus one person with significant control.

OFAC

The Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control keeps the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list and administers sanctions. Firms must screen customers and transactions against it. If a customer or counterparty is on the list, the firm must block (freeze) the property or reject the transaction, and report to OFAC within 10 business days. OFAC compliance applies to everyone in the U.S.; there is no minimum dollar amount.

Red flags

  • A customer who is reluctant to give identification.
  • Deposits of cash or money orders just under reporting thresholds.
  • Wires to or from high-risk jurisdictions with no business reason.
  • Deposits of securities followed quickly by withdrawal.
  • Activity out of line with the customer's stated profile.
  • A customer who shows no concern about losses or fees.
Trap: CTR is for cash over $10,000. SAR is for suspicious activity of $5,000 or more at a broker-dealer. Telling a customer a SAR was filed ("tipping off") is illegal.
keyPoints: BSA (1970) and USA PATRIOT Act Title III; FinCEN administers the rules; FINRA 3310 requires a written AML program with a compliance officer, training and independent testing.
Three stages: placement, layering (hiding the trail), integration.
CTR: cash of more than $10,000 in one business day (aggregated), filed within 15 calendar days.
SAR (broker-dealers): suspicious transactions of $5,000 or more, filed within 30 days of detection; never tell the customer.
Structuring cash to avoid a CTR is a federal crime even when the funds are legitimate.
CIP minimum: name, date of birth, street address and ID number, verified within a reasonable time.
OFAC: screen against the SDN list; block or reject and report within 10 business days; no dollar threshold.

topics.title: Privacy, Cybersecurity, Business Continuity & Senior Investors
topics.reading:
Regulation S-P: privacy of consumer information

Regulation S-P carries out the privacy provisions of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (1999) for broker-dealers, investment companies and SEC-registered advisers. State-registered advisers follow parallel FTC and state rules. It protects nonpublic personal information (NPI): personally identifiable financial information a customer provides or the firm obtains, such as account numbers, balances and Social Security numbers.

  • Initial privacy notice: given no later than when the customer relationship is established.
  • Annual privacy notice: given every year while the relationship continues, unless the firm qualifies for the annual-notice exception. The exception applies when the firm shares NPI only under the statutory exceptions (for example with service providers, to process transactions, or to comply with law) and has not changed its policies since its last notice.
  • Opt-out: before sharing NPI with nonaffiliated third parties outside those exceptions (for example, selling a client list to a marketer), the firm must give the customer an opt-out notice and a reasonable chance to opt out. Federal law uses opt-out, not opt-in. Separately, Regulation S-AM lets consumers opt out of affiliates' use of their information for marketing.
  • Safeguards rule: written policies and procedures with administrative, technical and physical safeguards to protect customer records and information. The disposal rule requires proper destruction of consumer report information.

2024 amendments to Regulation S-P

The SEC adopted amendments in May 2024. Compliance dates are December 2025 for larger entities and June 2026 for smaller ones. Covered firms must:

  • adopt a written incident response program reasonably designed to detect, respond to and recover from unauthorized access to or use of customer information;
  • notify affected individuals whose sensitive customer information was, or is reasonably likely to have been, accessed or used without authorization. Notice must be given as soon as practicable, but no later than 30 days after the firm becomes aware of the incident;
  • oversee service providers, which must notify the firm within 72 hours of a breach;
  • keep written records of compliance.

The amendments also wrote the annual-notice exception into the rule and extended the safeguards to information about customers of other financial institutions that the firm receives.

Regulation S-ID (the identity theft red flags rule) requires firms with covered accounts to keep a written identity theft prevention program. NASAA's model rules also treat failing to have written physical-security and cybersecurity policies as a problem for state-registered advisers.

Business continuity and succession planning

NASAA's model rule on business continuity and succession planning requires state-registered advisers to establish, implement and maintain written procedures that address:

  • protection, backup and recovery of books and records;
  • alternate ways to communicate with clients, key personnel, employees, vendors, service providers (including third-party custodians) and regulators;
  • office relocation after a temporary or permanent loss of a principal place of business;
  • assignment of duties to qualified responsible persons if key personnel die or become unavailable. This is the succession piece and is especially important for one-person firms.
  • otherwise minimizing service disruption and client harm.

Broker-dealers follow FINRA Rule 4370. It requires a written business continuity plan reviewed annually, two emergency contact persons (at least one a registered principal), and a summary of the plan disclosed to customers when they open an account, posted on the firm's website and mailed on request.

Senior and vulnerable adults

NASAA's Model Act to Protect Vulnerable Adults from Financial Exploitation (2016), adopted in many states, covers an eligible adult: a person 65 or older, or an adult covered by the state's adult protective services statute.

  • Reporting: a qualified individual (an agent, IAR, supervisor or compliance officer) who reasonably believes financial exploitation has occurred, is being attempted or has been attempted must promptly notify Adult Protective Services (APS) and the securities Administrator.
  • Third-party notice: the firm may notify a third party the client named earlier, such as a trusted contact, unless that person is suspected of the exploitation.
  • Delaying disbursements (temporary hold): the firm may delay a disbursement from the account if it reasonably believes exploitation is involved. It must notify all parties authorized on the account (except a suspected exploiter) in writing within 2 business days, and notify the Administrator and APS within 3 business days. The hold expires after 15 business days unless the Administrator or APS asks to extend it for up to 10 more business days, for 25 in total. A court can extend it further.
  • Immunity: good-faith reporting and delays are protected from administrative and civil liability. Firms must provide records to APS and law enforcement on request.

Under FINRA Rule 4512, broker-dealers must make reasonable efforts to get the name and contact information of a trusted contact person (age 18 or older) when an account is opened or updated. A customer who declines can still open the account. The trusted contact has no authority to trade. The firm may contact them to address suspected exploitation, confirm the customer's health or whereabouts, or identify a guardian or executor. FINRA Rule 2165 separately lets firms place temporary holds for "specified adults" (65 or older, or 18 or older with an impairment).

Exam tip: Hold numbers: 2 business days to notify, 15 business days for the hold, plus 10 more if the Administrator or APS extends it. Privacy: federal law is opt-out, and breach notices go out within 30 days.
keyPoints: Reg S-P: initial privacy notice when the relationship starts, and an annual notice unless the annual-notice exception applies.
Sharing NPI with nonaffiliated third parties outside the exceptions requires notice and a reasonable opportunity to opt out (not opt in).
2024 Reg S-P amendments: written incident response program; notify affected individuals no later than 30 days after becoming aware; service providers notify within 72 hours.
Safeguards rule requires written administrative, technical and physical safeguards; Reg S-ID requires an identity theft program.
NASAA BCP and succession model rule: written plans covering records backup, alternate communications, office relocation and replacement of key personnel.
NASAA vulnerable adult model act: eligible adult is 65+; report to APS and the Administrator; hold of 15 business days plus up to 10 more; notify account parties within 2 business days.
FINRA 4512 trusted contact: reasonable efforts to obtain one; the account may be opened without one; no trading authority.

flashcards.front: Three-prong test for an investment adviser
flashcards.back: (1) Advice about securities, (2) in the business of giving it, (3) for compensation. All three must be met.

flashcards.front: LATE exclusion
flashcards.back: Lawyers, Accountants, Teachers, and Engineers are not investment advisers if their advice is solely incidental to their profession. Charging separately or holding out as an adviser loses the exclusion.

flashcards.front: When is a broker-dealer excluded from the IA definition?
flashcards.back: When its advice is solely incidental to its brokerage business AND it receives no special compensation for the advice.

flashcards.front: Publisher exclusion
flashcards.back: Publishers of bona fide newspapers, news magazines, or financial publications of general, regular circulation giving impersonal advice are not investment advisers.

flashcards.front: Are federal covered advisers 'investment advisers' under the USA?
flashcards.back: No. The USA excludes federal covered advisers from the IA definition; states can only require notice filings and enforce antifraud rules.

flashcards.front: Excluded vs. exempt
flashcards.back: Excluded = not within the definition at all. Exempt = within the definition, but relieved of registration; antifraud rules still apply.

flashcards.front: AUM level at which an adviser MUST register with the SEC
flashcards.back: $110 million. Between $100M and $110M it may choose SEC registration; under $100M it generally registers with the state.

flashcards.front: Adviser to a registered investment company with $20M AUM registers where?
flashcards.back: With the SEC. Advisers to registered investment companies are federal covered regardless of AUM.

flashcards.front: What may a state require of a federal covered adviser?
flashcards.back: A notice filing: copies of documents filed with the SEC, a filing fee, and a consent to service of process.

flashcards.front: De minimis exemption for investment advisers
flashcards.back: No place of business in the state AND no more than 5 non-institutional resident clients in the preceding 12 months (NSMIA: fewer than 6).

flashcards.front: Private fund adviser exemption
flashcards.back: Adviser solely to private funds with less than $150 million in U.S. AUM is exempt from SEC registration but files as an exempt reporting adviser.

flashcards.front: Form ADV Part 2A vs. Part 2B
flashcards.back: 2A is the firm brochure (services, fees, conflicts). 2B is the brochure supplement about the individuals who give advice to the client.

flashcards.front: Deadline for Form ADV annual updating amendment
flashcards.back: Within 90 days after the end of the adviser's fiscal year.

flashcards.front: Brochure delivery timing (state rule)
flashcards.back: At least 48 hours before entering the contract, or at contract signing if the client may cancel without penalty within 5 business days.

flashcards.front: Minimum net worth: custody vs. discretion
flashcards.back: Custody: $35,000. Discretion without custody: $10,000. Prepayment of more than $500 six or more months in advance: positive net worth.

flashcards.front: How long must a state IA keep books and records?
flashcards.back: 5 years from the end of the fiscal year of the last entry, the first 2 years in an easily accessible place.

flashcards.front: Are federal covered advisers subject to state net worth requirements?
flashcards.back: No. NSMIA preempts state net worth, bonding, and books-and-records requirements beyond the SEC's.

flashcards.front: Five activities that make someone an IAR
flashcards.back: Gives advice/recommendations, manages accounts, determines which advice is given, solicits or sells advisory services, or supervises those who do.

flashcards.front: Form used to register an IAR or agent
flashcards.back: Form U4, filed through the CRD system. Form U5 reports termination.

flashcards.front: Where must an IAR of a federal covered adviser register?
flashcards.back: Only in states where the IAR has a place of business.

flashcards.front: Broker vs. dealer
flashcards.back: Broker = executes trades as agent for customers' accounts. Dealer = trades for its own account as principal.

flashcards.front: BD exclusion for firms with no place of business in the state
flashcards.back: Not a BD in the state if its only transactions there are with issuers, other broker-dealers, or institutional investors (plus certain existing customers temporarily in the state).

flashcards.front: Is there a 5-client de minimis rule for broker-dealers?
flashcards.back: No. A BD that sells to even one new non-institutional resident must register in that state.

flashcards.front: Agent definition
flashcards.back: An individual (never a firm) who represents a broker-dealer or issuer in effecting or attempting to effect securities transactions.

flashcards.front: Is a BD's employee selling Treasury bonds an agent?
flashcards.back: Yes. Anyone representing a BD in securities transactions is an agent, even for exempt securities. Only issuer representatives get the exempt-security exclusion.

flashcards.front: When is an issuer's representative NOT an agent?
flashcards.back: When selling certain exempt securities, in exempt transactions, or to the issuer's employees under a benefit plan with no commission paid.

flashcards.front: Can an agent represent two broker-dealers at once?
flashcards.back: Only if the BDs are affiliated through direct or indirect common control.

flashcards.front: Who notifies when an agent leaves a BD?
flashcards.back: Both the agent and the BD must promptly notify the Administrator. On a transfer, the old BD, new BD, and agent all notify.

flashcards.front: Howey test
flashcards.back: An investment of money in a common enterprise with an expectation of profits derived primarily from the efforts of others.

flashcards.front: Name four things that are NOT securities
flashcards.back: Fixed annuities/insurance policies, commodities and futures, collectibles (art, coins, gold held directly), and interests in a retirement plan such as a 401(k).

flashcards.front: Registration by coordination
flashcards.back: Used when the issuer is registering with the SEC under the 1933 Act; the state registration becomes effective when the federal registration does.

flashcards.front: Registration by qualification
flashcards.back: Used for securities not registered with the SEC (e.g., intrastate offerings); effective only when the Administrator orders it.

flashcards.front: Exempt security vs. exempt transaction
flashcards.back: Exempt security: exempt because of its issuer (government, municipal, bank, etc.). Exempt transaction: exempt because of the buyer or manner of sale (institutional, isolated, unsolicited, private placement).

flashcards.front: Commercial paper exemption requirements
flashcards.back: Prime quality (top three ratings), maturity of 9 months (270 days) or less, and denominations of at least $50,000.

flashcards.front: Private placement exemption (USA)
flashcards.back: Offers to no more than 10 non-institutional persons in the state in 12 months, reasonable belief of investment intent, no commission for soliciting non-institutional buyers.

flashcards.front: What can the Administrator NOT do on its own?
flashcards.back: Issue injunctions, impose criminal penalties (fines/prison), or enforce a subpoena — these require a court.

flashcards.front: Nonpunitive cancellation grounds
flashcards.back: Registrant no longer exists, has ceased doing business, cannot be located, or has been adjudicated mentally incompetent.

flashcards.front: Criminal penalty under the 1956 USA
flashcards.back: For willful violations: up to $5,000 fine, up to 3 years in prison, or both.

flashcards.front: Rescission recovery formula
flashcards.back: Purchase price + interest + court costs + reasonable attorney's fees − income (dividends/interest) received.

flashcards.front: Statute of limitations for civil suits (as tested)
flashcards.back: The earlier of 2 years after discovery of the violation or 3 years after the sale.

flashcards.front: Effect of a rescission offer
flashcards.back: If the buyer does not accept a written rescission offer within 30 days of receipt, the buyer loses the right to sue.

flashcards.front: When is an offer 'made' in a state?
flashcards.back: When it originates from the state, or is directed to the state and received there. Accepted when acceptance is communicated to the offeror in the state.

flashcards.front: Can an adviser say it is 'registered with the State Securities Division'?
flashcards.back: Yes. Stating the fact of registration is allowed. Saying or implying that the Administrator approved the firm, its strategy or any security is unlawful.

flashcards.front: Three provisions the USA requires in every advisory contract
flashcards.back: (1) No performance-based fee except as permitted (qualified clients); (2) no assignment without client consent; (3) a partnership IA will notify clients of changes in its membership within a reasonable time.

flashcards.front: Minority partner change vs change of control at an IA partnership
flashcards.back: A minority change is not an assignment; clients only need to be notified. A change of control (majority) is an assignment and requires client consent.

flashcards.front: Hedge clause
flashcards.back: A contract provision that tries to waive, or appears to waive, a client's rights under securities laws. It is prohibited, and any such waiver is void.

flashcards.front: IA books and records retention period
flashcards.back: 5 years from the end of the fiscal year of the last entry; the first 2 years in an appropriate office of the adviser. Electronic communications are included.

flashcards.front: Communications excluded from the SEC Marketing Rule's definition of 'advertisement'
flashcards.back: Extemporaneous, live, oral communications; one-on-one communications (unless they contain hypothetical performance); and information required by statute or regulation.

flashcards.front: Testimonial vs endorsement (SEC Marketing Rule)
flashcards.back: A testimonial comes from a current client; an endorsement comes from a non-client. Both are allowed with clear and prominent disclosure of client status, compensation and material conflicts.

flashcards.front: Rule for showing gross performance in an ad
flashcards.back: Net-of-fee performance must also be shown, with at least equal prominence, over the same period and calculated the same way.

flashcards.front: Required time periods for portfolio performance in an ad (non-private fund)
flashcards.back: 1-, 5- and 10-year periods (or the portfolio's life if shorter), each ending no earlier than the most recent calendar year-end.

flashcards.front: Adoption vs entanglement (third-party content)
flashcards.back: Adoption: the firm endorses or approves the content, for example by sharing, liking or commenting approvingly. Entanglement: the firm helped prepare it. Either way the firm is responsible for the content.

flashcards.front: Qualified client (for performance fees)
flashcards.back: At least $1.4M under management with the adviser, or net worth over $2.7M excluding the primary residence (also qualified purchasers). These SEC thresholds took effect June 29, 2026 (previously $1.1M/$2.2M); exam items may use the older figures.

flashcards.front: Section 28(e) soft dollars: what qualifies?
flashcards.back: Research and brokerage services that help investment decisions, such as research reports, analytical software and market data. Rent, furniture, travel, salaries and marketing do not qualify.

flashcards.front: Principal vs agency cross transaction: consent
flashcards.back: Principal: written disclosure of capacity and client consent before completion of each trade. Agency cross: blanket written consent is allowed, with per-trade confirmations and an annual summary, and it is revocable at any time.

flashcards.front: Who is a wrap fee account least suitable for?
flashcards.back: A buy-and-hold client who trades rarely. They pay a bundled fee for execution they don't use ('reverse churning').

flashcards.front: Is '1% of average quarterly AUM' a performance fee?
flashcards.back: No. A fee based on average asset value over a period is not a performance fee. Taking a share of gains, such as 20% of appreciation, is.

flashcards.front: Arrangements that give an adviser custody
flashcards.back: Possessing client assets; fee deduction; a general power of attorney; check-writing authority; a standing letter of authorization (SLOA) to third parties; passwords that allow withdrawals; serving as trustee or general partner.

flashcards.front: Inadvertent receipt of client securities
flashcards.back: Not custody if returned to the sender promptly, and in any case within 3 business days.

flashcards.front: Custody requirements (NASAA model rule)
flashcards.back: Notify the Administrator on Form ADV; use a qualified custodian; tell the client in writing where assets are held; custodian statements at least quarterly; an annual surprise exam by an independent CPA.

flashcards.front: How often must the surprise examination occur?
flashcards.back: At least once each calendar year, by an independent CPA, at a time chosen without notice. Advisers with custody only through fee deduction are generally exempt.

flashcards.front: NASAA minimum net worth: custody vs discretion
flashcards.back: $35,000 for an adviser with custody; $10,000 for an adviser with discretion but not custody.

flashcards.front: What counts as discretion?
flashcards.back: Deciding the asset, the action (buy or sell) or the amount. Deciding only time and/or price is not discretion.

flashcards.front: Written discretionary authority: IA vs BD agent
flashcards.back: IA or IAR: within 10 business days after the first discretionary trade (NASAA). BD agent: before the first discretionary trade.

flashcards.front: When does time-and-price discretion expire?
flashcards.back: At the end of the business day it was granted, unless the client provides written authorization otherwise (FINRA 3260).

flashcards.front: Limited trading authorization vs general power of attorney
flashcards.back: A limited trading authorization allows trading only: discretion, not custody. A general POA allowing withdrawals creates custody.

flashcards.front: When may an IAR borrow money from a client?
flashcards.back: Only if the client is a financial institution in the business of lending, such as a bank. The IA rules also allow borrowing from a BD or affiliate client. Borrowing from a friend or relative who is a client is prohibited.

flashcards.front: Conditions for an agent to share in a customer account's profits or losses
flashcards.back: Joint account; written authorization from the customer and the BD; sharing in proportion to the agent's own contribution (immediate family accounts are excepted).

flashcards.front: Selling away
flashcards.back: Effecting securities transactions not recorded on the BD's books. It is unethical unless the BD authorizes it in writing before execution.

flashcards.front: ITSFEA civil penalty
flashcards.back: Up to 3 times the profit gained or loss avoided. Controlling persons: up to the greater of $1 million (inflation-adjusted) or 3 times.

flashcards.front: Front running vs scalping
flashcards.back: Front running: trading ahead of a known customer block order. Scalping: an adviser buys a security, recommends it, then sells into the price rise.

flashcards.front: Components of an IA's duty of care
flashcards.back: Best-interest advice based on a reasonable understanding of the client, seeking best execution, and monitoring at a frequency consistent with the relationship.

flashcards.front: Duty of loyalty
flashcards.back: Never put the adviser's interests ahead of the client's. Make full and fair disclosure of all material facts and conflicts, and eliminate or disclose conflicts so the client can give informed consent.

flashcards.front: Regulation Best Interest's four obligations
flashcards.back: Disclosure, Care, Conflict of Interest and Compliance. They apply to BD recommendations to retail customers at the time a recommendation is made.

flashcards.front: Form CRS: length and IA delivery timing
flashcards.back: At most 2 pages (4 for dual registrants). An IA delivers it to retail investors before or at the time of entering into the advisory contract.

flashcards.front: Is it unethical to give a client a report prepared by someone else?
flashcards.back: Yes, unless you disclose that fact. The exception: using published research or statistical analyses, or ordering such a report in the normal course of business.

flashcards.front: Currency Transaction Report (CTR)
flashcards.back: Required for cash of more than $10,000 in one business day, including several transactions that add up to that amount. Filed with FinCEN within 15 calendar days.

flashcards.front: Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) for broker-dealers
flashcards.back: Suspicious transactions of $5,000 or more; filed within 30 calendar days of detection; the customer must never be told.

flashcards.front: Three stages of money laundering
flashcards.back: Placement (cash enters the system), layering (the trail is hidden through transactions), integration (the money returns as apparently legitimate funds).

flashcards.front: CIP minimum information for an individual
flashcards.back: Name, date of birth, street address and an identification number (TIN, or passport or other government ID for non-U.S. persons).

flashcards.front: Reg S-P privacy notices
flashcards.back: An initial notice when the customer relationship is established and an annual notice after that, unless the annual-notice exception applies (sharing only under exceptions, no policy changes). Customers may opt out of sharing with nonaffiliated third parties.

flashcards.front: 2024 Reg S-P amendments: breach notice deadline
flashcards.back: Affected individuals must be notified as soon as practicable, but no later than 30 days after the firm becomes aware of unauthorized access to sensitive customer information. An incident response program is also required.

flashcards.front: NASAA business continuity and succession planning model rule
flashcards.back: State-registered IAs must have written procedures for records backup, alternate communications, office relocation and replacement of key personnel if they die or become unavailable.

flashcards.front: NASAA temporary hold for an eligible adult (65+)
flashcards.back: The firm may delay a disbursement if exploitation is suspected. It notifies authorized parties within 2 business days. The hold lasts 15 business days, extendable up to 10 more at the request of the Administrator or APS.

questions.q: Which of the following persons is an investment adviser under the Uniform Securities Act?
choices: An attorney who, while drafting a client's will, recommends that assets be placed in a trust
A CPA who advertises a separate service recommending retirement portfolios of mutual funds and charges a flat fee for it
The trust department of a national bank that manages securities portfolios for customers
The publisher of a weekly financial newspaper of general and regular circulation
questions.explanation: The accountant's securities advice is no longer solely incidental to accounting — it is advertised and separately compensated — so the LATE exclusion is lost. The attorney's advice is incidental to legal practice, banks are excluded from the definition, and a bona fide publication of general, regular circulation is excluded.

questions.q:
Which of the following are EXCLUDED from the definition of investment adviser under the Uniform Securities Act?
I. A high school teacher who explains price-earnings ratios in an economics class
II. A broker-dealer that charges clients a separate fee for a written financial plan
III. The publisher of a nationally circulated financial magazine
IV. A savings institution
choices: I and II
I, III and IV
II and IV
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation: Teachers giving incidental advice (I), bona fide publishers of general circulation (III), and banks/savings institutions (IV) are excluded. A broker-dealer is excluded only if its advice is solely incidental to brokerage AND it receives no special compensation; a separate fee for a financial plan is special compensation, so II is an investment adviser.

questions.q: A broker-dealer's registered agents have always provided investment recommendations to customers, compensated solely through commissions on trades. The firm now plans to charge an annual fee for comprehensive financial planning that includes securities recommendations. Which statement is correct?
choices: The firm remains excluded because its advice is still related to its brokerage business
The firm remains excluded because its agents are registered with the state
The firm will receive special compensation for advice and will therefore meet the definition of an investment adviser
Only the individual agents, not the firm, would need to register as investment advisers
questions.explanation: The broker-dealer exclusion has two conditions: advice solely incidental to the brokerage business AND no special compensation. A separate financial-planning fee is special compensation, so the firm becomes an investment adviser. The agents would need IAR registration, but that doesn't relieve the firm.

questions.q: An individual gives clients specific recommendations about which stocks to buy but charges no separate fee. She is compensated only through commissions when clients purchase the securities she recommends. Regarding the compensation prong of the investment adviser definition, which is TRUE?
choices: It is not met, because no separate advisory fee is charged
It is met only if commissions exceed $500 per client per year
It is met, because compensation includes any economic benefit, including commissions
It is not met unless the client signs a written advisory contract
questions.explanation: Under SEC Release IA-1092, the compensation element is satisfied by the receipt of any economic benefit, whether an advisory fee, a commission, or some combination. There is no dollar threshold and no requirement for a written contract.

questions.q: Each of the following is excluded from the definition of investment adviser under the Uniform Securities Act EXCEPT
choices: an engineer whose advice on securities is solely incidental to the practice of engineering
a trust company
a federal covered adviser
a publisher of a newsletter sent to a select list of subscribers only when the publisher sees a market event that calls for specific buy or sell action
questions.explanation: The publisher exclusion requires a bona fide publication of general and regular circulation giving impersonal advice. A newsletter issued irregularly, timed to specific market events, and sent to a select list is not a bona fide publication, so its publisher is an investment adviser. Engineers (incidental), trust companies, and federal covered advisers are excluded under the USA.

questions.q: Under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, which of the following is EXCLUDED from the definition of investment adviser?
choices: A firm that manages the portfolio of a registered open-end investment company
A financial planner who charges hourly fees for recommending mutual funds
A sports agent who is paid to recommend common stocks to athletes
A person whose advice relates solely to securities issued or guaranteed by the U.S. government
questions.explanation: The IAA specifically excludes persons whose advice relates only to U.S. government securities. Advisers to registered investment companies must register with the SEC, and planners and sports agents who are paid for securities advice meet the three-prong test.

questions.q: An investment adviser with $105 million in regulatory assets under management does not advise any registered investment company. Which statement is correct?
choices: It must register with the SEC
It may register with the SEC but is not required to do so
It is prohibited from registering with the SEC
It must register with both the SEC and every state in which it has clients
questions.explanation: Advisers with between $100 million and $110 million in AUM are in a buffer zone: they may choose SEC registration but are not required to register with the SEC until they reach $110 million. Registration with the SEC would make it a federal covered adviser subject only to state notice filing.

questions.q: An investment adviser manages $30 million, all of which is the portfolio of a mutual fund registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940. The adviser must register with
choices: the state where it has its principal office only
each state in which fund shareholders reside
the SEC
no one, because mutual fund advisers are excluded
questions.explanation: Advisers to registered investment companies are federal covered advisers and must register with the SEC regardless of the amount of assets under management. States may require only a notice filing.

questions.q: An investment adviser registered in State A has no place of business in State B. During the last 12 months it had the following clients who are residents of State B: 4 individuals, 2 insurance companies, and 1 bank. Regarding State B, the adviser
choices: is not required to register, because it has no place of business there and no more than 5 non-institutional clients
must register, because it has 7 clients in State B
must register, because any individual client requires registration
is not required to register, but its IARs must register in State B
questions.explanation: Under the de minimis exemption, an adviser with no place of business in the state need not register if it has had no more than 5 resident clients in 12 months, not counting institutional clients such as insurance companies and banks. Here only 4 clients count. Because the firm is exempt, its IARs need not register there either.

questions.q:
Which of the following state-regulated investment advisers must register in State Z?
I. An adviser with an office in State Z and one client there
II. An adviser with no place of business in State Z that had 5 individual clients residing there over the last 12 months
III. An adviser with no place of business in State Z whose only clients there are pension plans and insurance companies
IV. An adviser with no place of business in State Z that had 7 individual clients residing there over the last 12 months
choices: I and II
I and IV
II and III
III and IV
questions.explanation: An adviser with a place of business in the state must register regardless of client count (I). With no place of business, an adviser is exempt if it has no more than 5 non-institutional resident clients (II is exempt) or only institutional clients (III is exempt). Seven individual clients exceeds the de minimis limit (IV must register).

questions.q:
A State Administrator may require which of the following from a federal covered adviser doing business in the state?
I. A notice filing consisting of copies of documents filed with the SEC
II. A filing fee
III. A minimum net worth of $35,000 if it has custody
IV. A consent to service of process
choices: I, II and IV
I and II only
II and III
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation: NSMIA limits states to requiring a notice filing (copies of SEC filings), fees, and a consent to service of process from federal covered advisers. States cannot impose their own net worth, bonding, or books-and-records requirements on SEC-registered advisers.

questions.q: An adviser manages $140 million, all in private funds (hedge funds), and has no other clients. Under federal law, the adviser
choices: must register with the SEC because its AUM exceeds $110 million
is exempt from SEC registration but must file reports with the SEC as an exempt reporting adviser
is excluded from the definition of investment adviser
must register with the SEC as a federal covered adviser but is exempt from Form ADV
questions.explanation: Advisers solely to private funds with less than $150 million in U.S. AUM qualify for the private fund adviser exemption. They are exempt reporting advisers: not registered, but they file portions of Form ADV. They are still investment advisers — exempt, not excluded — and may be subject to state registration.

questions.q: An investment adviser registered in State A, with $20 million under management, opens a branch office in State B, where it has 2 individual clients. Which statement is correct?
choices: The adviser is exempt in State B because it has fewer than 6 clients there
The adviser must register in State B
The adviser must register with the SEC because it now operates in two states
The adviser need only notice file in State B
questions.explanation: The de minimis exemption is available only to an adviser with NO place of business in the state. Once the adviser opens an office in State B, it must register there regardless of how few clients it has. Operating in two states does not trigger SEC registration, and notice filing applies only to federal covered advisers.

questions.q: An adviser has been registered with the SEC for several years. At the end of its most recent fiscal year, its regulatory assets under management declined from $120 million to $95 million. Which statement is correct?
choices: It must withdraw from SEC registration and register with the states within 90 days
It may remain registered with the SEC because its AUM has not fallen below $90 million
It must register with the states, since its AUM is now below $100 million
It must register with both the SEC and the states until AUM rises above $110 million
questions.explanation: To prevent advisers from switching back and forth, an SEC-registered adviser is not required to withdraw and register with the states unless its AUM falls below $90 million, as reported in its annual updating amendment. At $95 million it may stay with the SEC.

questions.q: A state-registered investment adviser delivers its Form ADV Part 2A brochure to a new client at the time the advisory contract is signed rather than 48 hours in advance. This is permissible only if
choices: the client signs a waiver of the 48-hour requirement
the client may terminate the contract without penalty within 5 business days
the brochure is also mailed to the Administrator the same day
the client may terminate the contract without penalty within 30 days
questions.explanation: The brochure rule requires delivery at least 48 hours before entering the contract, or at the time of contract if the client has the right to terminate without penalty within 5 business days. A client waiver would be void — any condition waiving compliance with the Act is void.

questions.q: Under NASAA's model rule, a state-registered investment adviser that has both custody of client funds and discretionary authority over client accounts must maintain a minimum net worth of
questions.explanation: The custody requirement ($35,000) is the higher standard and governs. The requirements are not added together; discretion alone requires $10,000, but an adviser with custody needs $35,000 whether or not it also has discretion.

questions.q: A state-registered adviser exercises discretion over client accounts but does not have custody. Its net worth is $6,000. To comply with NASAA's model rule, the adviser may
choices: obtain a surety bond of $4,000
obtain a surety bond of $10,000
obtain a surety bond of $5,000
continue operating as long as it notifies clients in writing
questions.explanation: Discretion requires a $10,000 net worth. An adviser that does not meet the requirement may post a bond equal to the deficiency rounded up to the nearest $5,000. The deficiency is $4,000 ($10,000 − $6,000), which rounds up to $5,000.

questions.q: Under NASAA's model rule, which state-registered adviser must maintain a positive net worth at all times but is NOT subject to the $10,000 or $35,000 minimum?
choices: An adviser with discretionary authority that bills fees quarterly in arrears
An adviser with no custody or discretion that collects a $1,000 annual fee from each client 12 months in advance
An adviser that holds client securities in its own name
An adviser with no custody or discretion that collects a $300 annual fee 12 months in advance
questions.explanation: An adviser that accepts prepayment of more than $500 per client, 6 or more months in advance, must maintain a positive net worth. The $300 prepayment does not meet the $500 threshold. Discretion triggers $10,000, and holding client securities is custody, which triggers $35,000.

questions.q: An investment adviser's annual updating amendment to Form ADV must be filed within
choices: 30 days after the end of the adviser's fiscal year
90 days after the end of the calendar year, regardless of fiscal year
120 days after the adviser's registration anniversary
90 days after the end of the adviser's fiscal year
questions.explanation: The annual updating amendment to Form ADV is due within 90 days of the adviser's fiscal year-end. Other material changes must be amended promptly. (Under SEC rules, the summary of material changes or updated brochure goes to clients within 120 days of fiscal year-end — a different requirement.)

questions.q: A state-registered investment adviser must retain its books and records for
choices: 3 years, the first 2 in an easily accessible place
6 years, the first 3 in an easily accessible place
2 years, all in the principal office
5 years, the first 2 in an easily accessible place
questions.explanation: Advisers keep books and records for 5 years from the end of the fiscal year of the last entry, with the first 2 years in an easily accessible place (the principal office). The 3-years/first-2 standard is the typical broker-dealer requirement.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements about a state-registered adviser's Form ADV Part 2A brochure are TRUE?
I. It may be delivered at least 48 hours before the client enters into the advisory contract
II. It may be delivered when the contract is signed if the client can cancel within 5 business days without penalty
III. It must be approved by the Administrator as to its merits before it is given to clients
IV. Each year the adviser must deliver an updated brochure, or a summary of material changes with an offer to provide the brochure
choices: I and III
II and III
I, II and IV
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation: Statements I, II and IV describe the delivery requirements (the annual update is due within 120 days of fiscal year-end). The Administrator does not approve or pass on the merits of a brochure; representing that the Administrator has approved any filing would itself be unlawful.

questions.q:
Which of the following employees of an investment adviser would be required to register as investment adviser representatives?
I. A receptionist who schedules client appointments
II. An employee paid to solicit new advisory clients
III. A manager who supervises the firm's portfolio managers
IV. An assistant who types and formats research reports
choices: I and II
I and IV
III and IV
II and III
questions.explanation: IARs include individuals who solicit or sell advisory services (II) and those who supervise individuals who give advice or manage accounts (III). Receptionists and typists perform clerical or ministerial functions and are not IARs.

questions.q: An IAR of a federal covered adviser works in the firm's only office, located in State A. She also has clients residing in States B and C but has no place of business in either. She must register as an IAR in
choices: States A, B, and C
State A only
States B and C only, if she has more than 5 clients in each
no state, because her firm is registered with the SEC
questions.explanation: Under NSMIA, a state may require an IAR of a federal covered adviser to register only if the IAR has a place of business in that state. She has a place of business only in State A. SEC registration of the firm does not cover the individual.

questions.q: When an investment adviser representative of a state-registered investment adviser terminates employment, who must promptly notify the Administrator?
choices: The IAR only
The SEC
The investment adviser
The client's custodian
questions.explanation: Under the USA, when an IAR of a state-registered adviser begins or terminates association, the investment adviser must promptly notify the Administrator. (Compare agents, where both the agent and the BD must notify.)

questions.q: A state-registered investment adviser hires an individual whose job will be to meet prospective clients and persuade them to sign advisory contracts, for which he will be paid a bonus. Before he begins, which is TRUE?
choices: He need not register because he does not give investment advice
He need not register because he is compensated by bonus rather than commission
He must register as an agent of a broker-dealer
He must be registered as an investment adviser representative
questions.explanation: Soliciting, offering, or negotiating for the sale of advisory services is one of the activities that makes an individual an IAR, even if he never gives advice. It is unlawful for the adviser to employ him before he is registered. He sells advisory services, not securities, so agent registration is not the issue.

questions.q: A registered agent of a broker-dealer begins providing financial planning, including securities recommendations, for a separate fee through the broker-dealer's affiliated state-registered investment adviser. Which is TRUE?
choices: He must also register as an investment adviser representative
His agent registration covers the new activity
He is excluded because his advice is incidental to his work as an agent
Only the affiliated adviser needs to register; he does not
questions.explanation: Agent and IAR registrations are separate. Once the individual provides advice for a separate fee on behalf of an investment adviser, he is an IAR and must register as one. The incidental-advice exclusion does not apply when special compensation is received.

questions.q:
Which of the following is a broker-dealer under the Uniform Securities Act?
I. A national bank
II. A corporation selling its own newly issued shares
III. A firm with an office in the state that executes trades for retail customers
IV. A firm with no office in the state whose only customers in the state are insurance companies
choices: III only
I and II
III and IV
I, III and IV
questions.explanation: Banks (I) and issuers (II) are excluded from the BD definition. A firm with no place of business in the state whose only customers there are institutional investors (IV) is also excluded. Only the firm with a local office serving retail customers (III) is a broker-dealer in the state.

questions.q: A broker-dealer registered only in State A has no place of business in State B. It solicits and makes a sale to one new individual customer residing in State B. Which is TRUE?
choices: No registration was required because it had fewer than 6 customers in State B
No registration was required because it has no place of business in State B
Only the agent, not the broker-dealer, was required to register in State B
The broker-dealer was required to be registered in State B
questions.explanation: There is no de minimis exemption for broker-dealers. A BD with no place of business in a state is excluded only if it deals exclusively with issuers, other BDs, institutional investors, or qualifying existing customers temporarily in the state. A sale to a new individual resident requires both the BD and its agent to be registered in State B.

questions.q: A broker-dealer registered in State A, with no office in State B, has an existing individual customer who resides in State A. While the customer is on a short vacation in State B, she calls the firm and places an order. Which is TRUE?
choices: The firm may accept the order without registering in State B
The firm must register in State B before accepting the order
The firm may accept the order only if the customer is an accredited investor
The firm must refuse the order until the customer returns to State A
questions.explanation: The Uniform Securities Act excludes from the BD definition in a state a firm with no place of business there that deals with an existing customer who is only temporarily present in the state, when the firm is registered in the customer's home state. This accommodates vacationing clients.

questions.q: A State Administrator wishes to require broker-dealers in the state to maintain net capital higher than the SEC requires. Under NSMIA, the Administrator
choices: may impose them if adopted by rule after public comment
may impose them only on broker-dealers with a principal office in the state
may impose them only if the Administrator holds a hearing
may not impose net capital requirements that exceed those of the SEC
questions.explanation: NSMIA prohibits states from imposing net capital, custody, margin, financial responsibility, books-and-records, or financial reporting requirements on broker-dealers that differ from or exceed the SEC's.

questions.q: A firm that stands ready to buy and sell a particular security for its own account, continuously quoting bid and ask prices, is a(n)
choices: underwriter
investment adviser
market maker
transfer agent
questions.explanation: A market maker is a dealer that maintains two-sided quotes and trades from its own inventory. An underwriter buys securities from an issuer for distribution; an investment adviser gives advice for compensation; a transfer agent maintains ownership records.

questions.q: Under SEC rules, which the states may not exceed, most broker-dealer records such as order tickets and customer communications must be kept for at least
choices: 5 years, the first 2 in an easily accessible place
1 year in the principal office
3 years, the first 2 in an easily accessible place
10 years, the first 5 in an easily accessible place
questions.explanation: Most BD records must be preserved for at least 3 years, the first 2 readily accessible (certain records, such as blotters and ledgers, for 6 years). The 5-year/first-2 standard applies to investment advisers.

questions.q: Which of the following individuals is an agent under the Uniform Securities Act?
choices: An employee of a broker-dealer who sells municipal bonds to retail customers
An officer of a corporation who sells its commercial paper to institutional investors without commission
A broker-dealer's receptionist who only answers phones
An issuer's employee who offers company stock to fellow employees under a benefit plan with no commission
questions.explanation: An individual representing a broker-dealer in securities transactions is always an agent, even when the securities (municipal bonds) are exempt. Individuals representing an issuer are excluded when selling certain exempt securities (commercial paper) or in no-commission employee plans, and clerical personnel are not agents.

questions.q:
Which of the following individuals is NOT an agent under the Uniform Securities Act?
I. A broker-dealer employee who sells U.S. Treasury bills to individual customers
II. An issuer's treasurer who sells the issuer's prime-rated, 90-day commercial paper, receiving no commission
III. An issuer's employee who offers issuer stock to other employees under an employee benefit plan, receiving no commission
IV. An issuer's employee who sells the issuer's stock to the public in a registered offering for a commission
choices: II and III
I and II
I and IV
III and IV
questions.explanation: An individual representing an issuer is not an agent when selling certain exempt securities such as qualifying commercial paper (II) or when offering securities to employees under a benefit plan without commission (III). Someone representing a broker-dealer (I) is always an agent, and an issuer's representative in a non-exempt public offering (IV) is an agent.

questions.q: An agent may be registered to represent more than one broker-dealer at the same time only if
choices: each broker-dealer consents in writing
the broker-dealers are affiliated through direct or indirect common control
the agent is registered in fewer than 6 states
the Administrator approves each transaction in advance
questions.explanation: Under the USA, an agent may represent only one broker-dealer or issuer at a time unless they are affiliated by direct or indirect common control. Consent of the firms alone is not enough.

questions.q: When a registered agent terminates employment with a broker-dealer, who is required to promptly notify the Administrator?
choices: The broker-dealer only
The agent only
Both the agent and the broker-dealer
The SEC
questions.explanation: Under the USA, when an agent begins or terminates a connection with a broker-dealer or issuer, both the agent and the broker-dealer (or issuer) must promptly notify the Administrator. The termination is reported through CRD on Form U5.

questions.q:
An agent transfers from Broker-Dealer A to Broker-Dealer B. Who must notify the Administrator?
I. The agent
II. Broker-Dealer A
III. Broker-Dealer B
IV. The issuers of securities the agent previously sold
choices: I and II
II and III
I, II, III and IV
I, II and III
questions.explanation: In a transfer, the terminating firm (A), the hiring firm (B), and the agent must all notify the Administrator. Issuers of securities the agent sold have no notification obligation.

questions.q: An agent is terminated by his broker-dealer on March 1 and joins a new broker-dealer on March 20. On March 10, an existing customer asks him to buy shares for her. Which is TRUE?
choices: He may effect the transaction because the customer is an existing client
He may effect the transaction if it is unsolicited
He may effect the transaction as long as he notifies the Administrator within 30 days
He may not effect the transaction, because his registration is not effective while he is not associated with a broker-dealer
questions.explanation: An agent's registration is not effective during any period in which the agent is not associated with a registered broker-dealer or issuer. Between March 1 and the effective date of his new association, he cannot act as an agent for anyone.

questions.q: A broker-dealer is registered in States A and B. One of its agents is registered only in State A. The agent calls a new individual prospect who lives in State B and completes a sale of listed stock. Which is TRUE?
choices: No violation occurred because the broker-dealer is registered in State B
No violation occurred because the stock is a federal covered security
The agent violated the Uniform Securities Act by transacting business in State B without being registered there
No violation occurred because the call originated in State A
questions.explanation: Registration of the broker-dealer does not register its individual agents. The agent transacted business with a non-institutional resident of State B and needed his own registration there. The security's federal covered status exempts it from security registration, not the agent from agent registration. An offer directed to and received in State B is made in State B.

questions.q:
Which of the following are NOT securities under the Uniform Securities Act?
I. A variable annuity
II. A fixed annuity
III. A commodity futures contract
IV. A fractional undivided interest in an oil and gas drilling program
choices: I and II
I and IV
III and IV
II and III
questions.explanation: Fixed annuities (insurance contracts with a guaranteed payout) and commodity futures contracts are not securities. Variable annuities are securities because the investment risk falls on the purchaser, and fractional interests in oil, gas, or mineral rights are specifically listed in the definition of security.

questions.q: Each of the following is an element of the Howey test for an investment contract EXCEPT
choices: an investment of money
a common enterprise
a written agreement signed by the investor
an expectation of profits derived primarily from the efforts of others
questions.explanation: The Howey test asks whether there is an investment of money in a common enterprise with an expectation of profits derived primarily from the efforts of others. No written contract is required; oral arrangements can be investment contracts.

questions.q: An issuer is filing a registration statement with the SEC under the Securities Act of 1933 and wants the offering registered in several states at the same time. The appropriate method of state registration is
choices: qualification
coordination
notification
notice filing as a federal covered security
questions.explanation: Registration by coordination is used when a federal registration statement has been filed under the 1933 Act; the state registration becomes effective simultaneously with the federal registration if conditions are met. Qualification is for offerings not registered federally, and a new unlisted offering is not automatically a federal covered security.

questions.q: A new company plans to raise capital by selling stock only to residents of its home state and will not register the offering with the SEC. Under the Uniform Securities Act, the offering would be registered by
choices: qualification
coordination
notification
notice filing
questions.explanation: Qualification is available for any security and is the method used when there is no federal registration, such as an intrastate offering. It becomes effective only when the Administrator so orders. Coordination requires a concurrent SEC registration, and notification is for established issuers with an operating and earnings history.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a federal covered security?
choices: Stock of a start-up company sold in an intrastate offering not listed on any exchange
Common stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange
Shares of an open-end investment company registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940
Securities sold in a Rule 506 private placement under Regulation D
questions.explanation: Federal covered securities include exchange-listed securities, registered investment company securities, and Rule 506 offerings, among others. An unlisted intrastate offering is not federal covered and would have to be registered in the state (typically by qualification) unless exempt.

questions.q:
Regarding a federal covered security offered in the state, the Administrator may
I. require a notice filing
II. require payment of a filing fee
III. require registration by coordination
IV. bring an action for fraud in connection with its sale
choices: I and III
I, II and IV
II and III
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation: States may not require registration of federal covered securities, but they may require notice filings and fees, and they retain antifraud authority over all securities transactions.

questions.q:
Which of the following are exempt securities under the Uniform Securities Act?
I. General obligation bonds issued by a city in another state
II. A certificate of deposit issued by a national bank
III. Commercial paper rated in the highest category with a 12-month maturity, in $100,000 denominations
IV. Bonds issued by the government of Canada
choices: I and III
II and III
I, II, III and IV
I, II and IV
questions.explanation: Municipal securities of any state or its subdivisions (I), bank securities (II), and Canadian government securities (IV) are exempt securities. Commercial paper qualifies only if its maturity is 9 months (270 days) or less, so the 12-month note (III) is not exempt.

questions.q: Which of the following is an exempt TRANSACTION rather than an exempt security?
choices: The sale of an unregistered, non-exempt corporate stock to an insurance company
The sale of a U.S. Treasury bond to an individual
The sale of a bond issued by a church to a parishioner
The sale of revenue bonds issued by a state turnpike authority
questions.explanation: Sales to institutional investors (banks, insurance companies, investment companies, etc.) are exempt transactions — the exemption comes from the buyer, not the security. Treasury, nonprofit, and municipal securities are exempt securities because of the nature of their issuers.

questions.q: During a 12-month period, an issuer offers unregistered, non-exempt securities to 12 individuals in the state, none of whom are institutional investors. Only 4 of them purchase. No commissions are paid, and all buyers purchase for investment. Which is TRUE?
choices: The private placement exemption is not available because more than 10 persons received offers
The private placement exemption is available because only 4 persons purchased
The private placement exemption is available because no commissions were paid
The transaction is exempt as an isolated nonissuer transaction
questions.explanation: The USA private placement exemption limits OFFERS to no more than 10 non-institutional persons in the state in 12 months. Offering to 12 individuals exceeds the limit regardless of how many buy. It is not a nonissuer transaction because the issuer is the seller.

questions.q: During a 12-month period, an issuer offers unregistered securities in the state to 8 individuals and 20 institutional investors. No commissions are paid for soliciting anyone, and the issuer reasonably believes all purchasers are buying for investment. The offering is
choices: not exempt, because 28 persons received offers
exempt only if it is also registered by coordination
not exempt, because an issuer can never rely on a transaction exemption
exempt as a private placement, because institutional offerees are not counted toward the 10-person limit
questions.explanation: Institutional investors are not counted toward the 10-offeree limit, so only the 8 individuals count. With no commissions paid for soliciting non-institutional buyers and investment intent, the private placement exemption is available.

questions.q:
Which of the following are exempt transactions under the Uniform Securities Act?
I. An executor selling stock from a decedent's estate
II. A bank selling securities pledged as loan collateral after the borrower defaults
III. An agent soliciting retail customers to buy unregistered, non-exempt stock from the firm's inventory
IV. An issuer selling its securities to an underwriter
choices: I, II and IV
I and III
II and III
III and IV
questions.explanation: Transactions by fiduciaries such as executors (I), sales by a bona fide pledgee of collateral (II), and transactions between an issuer and an underwriter (IV) are exempt transactions. Soliciting retail customers to buy unregistered, non-exempt securities (III) fits no exemption.

questions.q: An agent sells municipal bonds to a client and makes misleading statements about the issuer's financial condition. Which is TRUE?
