choices: No violation occurred because municipal bonds are exempt securities
The antifraud provisions of the Uniform Securities Act apply even though the bonds are exempt from registration
Only the SEC has jurisdiction because municipal bonds are federal covered
The Administrator may act only if the bonds were issued by a municipality in that state
questions.explanation: Exemption from registration never means exemption from the antifraud provisions. The Administrator has antifraud authority over all securities and transactions, including exempt and federal covered ones, regardless of where the issuer is located.

questions.q: Under the Investment Company Act of 1940, which type of investment company is organized under a trust indenture, has no board of directors, and issues redeemable units in a fixed portfolio?
choices: Face-amount certificate company
Open-end management company
Closed-end management company
Unit investment trust
questions.explanation: A UIT is organized under a trust indenture, has no board of directors or investment adviser actively managing it, and issues redeemable units in a generally fixed portfolio. Face-amount certificate companies issue debt certificates; management companies (open- or closed-end) are actively managed and have boards.

questions.q: Which of the following would qualify as exempt commercial paper under the Uniform Securities Act?
choices: A note rated in the highest rating category, maturing in 12 months, issued in $100,000 denominations
An unrated note maturing in 90 days, issued in $50,000 denominations
A note rated in the highest rating category, maturing in 60 days, issued in $10,000 denominations
A note rated in the highest rating category, maturing in 180 days, issued in $100,000 denominations
questions.explanation: Exempt commercial paper must be prime quality (one of the three highest rating categories), mature in 9 months (270 days) or less, and be issued in denominations of at least $50,000. Only the 180-day, top-rated, $100,000 note meets all three conditions.

questions.q: Under the Uniform Securities Act, the Administrator may do each of the following EXCEPT
choices: issue a cease and desist order
issue an injunction prohibiting a firm from selling securities
conduct an investigation outside the state
issue subpoenas to compel testimony
questions.explanation: The Administrator may issue cease and desist orders, investigate inside or outside the state, and issue subpoenas. An injunction is a court order; the Administrator must go to court to obtain one.

questions.q:
Which of the following are grounds for the Administrator to deny an application for agent registration, if in the public interest?
I. The applicant was convicted of a felony unrelated to securities 7 years ago
II. The application contains a materially misleading statement
III. The applicant has no experience, although she is qualified by training and knowledge
IV. The applicant is insolvent
choices: I and III
I, II and IV
II and III
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation: A conviction for any felony within the past 10 years (I), a materially false or misleading application (II), and insolvency (IV) are grounds for denial. Lack of experience alone is not a ground when the applicant is qualified by training or knowledge (III).

questions.q: Which statement about a summary cease and desist order issued by the Administrator is TRUE?
choices: It may be issued without a prior hearing, but the respondent must be given an opportunity for a hearing
It may be issued only after a full hearing
It must be approved by a court before it becomes effective
It is final and cannot be challenged by the respondent
questions.explanation: A summary order takes effect immediately, without prior notice or hearing, to protect investors. The Administrator must then promptly notify the respondent and offer an opportunity for a hearing, after which the order may be vacated, modified, or made final.

questions.q: Under the Uniform Securities Act of 1956, a person convicted of willfully violating the Act may be
choices: fined up to $10,000, imprisoned up to 5 years, or both
fined up to $5,000, but not imprisoned
fined up to $5,000, imprisoned up to 3 years, or both
imprisoned up to 3 years only if the violation involved more than $5,000
questions.explanation: The 1956 Act provides criminal penalties of up to $5,000, up to 3 years, or both for each willful violation. Criminal penalties are imposed by a court, not the Administrator, and require willfulness.

questions.q: A customer bought 1,000 shares at $20 per share from an agent who was not registered. While holding the shares, she received $600 in dividends. She sues for rescission; interest at the legal rate is $1,000 and her reasonable attorney's fees are $2,500. How much may she recover (assuming she tenders the shares)?
questions.explanation: Rescission recovery = purchase price + interest + costs and attorney's fees − income received: $20,000 + $1,000 + $2,500 − $600 = $22,900. $23,500 forgets to subtract the dividends; $21,400 leaves out attorney's fees; $19,400 is simply price less dividends.

questions.q: A client purchased a security on January 10, 2022, from an agent who made a material misrepresentation. The client discovered the misrepresentation on March 1, 2024. Under the civil liability provisions as tested, the client must file suit no later than
choices: January 10, 2025
March 1, 2026
January 10, 2024
March 1, 2027
questions.explanation: The limitation period is the earlier of 2 years after discovery (March 1, 2026) or 3 years after the sale (January 10, 2025). The earlier date, January 10, 2025, controls.

questions.q: A broker-dealer sold a customer an unregistered, non-exempt security. Discovering the error, the firm sends the customer a written offer to repurchase the security for the purchase price plus interest, less income received. The customer ignores the offer for 45 days. Which is TRUE?
choices: The customer has lost the right to sue for rescission
The customer may still sue within 3 years of the sale
The offer is void because it did not include attorney's fees
The customer may sue only for damages equal to the firm's commission
questions.explanation: A buyer who receives a written rescission offer and fails to accept it within 30 days of receipt loses the right to bring a civil suit. The offer need not include attorney's fees because no suit has yet been brought.

questions.q: An agent in State A telephones a client who lives in State C while the client is vacationing in State B, and offers him a security. The client accepts the offer during the call. Which State Administrators have jurisdiction over the transaction?
choices: State A only
State C only
States A and B
States B and C
questions.explanation: An offer is made in a state when it originates from that state (State A) or is directed to and received in that state (State B). Acceptance is communicated to the offeror in State A. The client's home state (C) is not involved because the offer was neither made from nor received in State C.

questions.q: A securities offering is advertised in a bona fide newspaper published in State X that has had more than two-thirds of its circulation outside State X during the past 12 months. Under the Uniform Securities Act, the advertisement
choices: is considered an offer made in every state where the paper circulates
is considered an offer made only in State X
is not considered an offer made in State X
requires registration of the security in State X before publication
questions.explanation: An offer is not deemed made in a state merely because it appears in a bona fide newspaper published outside the state, or published inside the state but with more than two-thirds of its circulation outside the state during the past 12 months.

questions.q: An investment adviser registered in State X includes this sentence in its brochure: "Our firm is registered with the State X Securities Division, which has reviewed and approved our investment strategy." This statement is:
choices: permissible, as long as the firm's registration is current and effective
unlawful, because it implies that the Administrator has passed on the merits of the adviser's services
unlawful only if clients later lose money following the strategy
permissible, because the firm is in fact registered in State X
questions.explanation: Stating the fact of registration is allowed, but saying or implying that the Administrator reviewed or approved the adviser, its services or a security is an unlawful representation under the USA. Being currently registered does not make the 'approved' language acceptable, and the violation does not depend on how the strategy performs.

questions.q: Under the Uniform Securities Act, an investment advisory contract must provide for each of the following EXCEPT:
choices: that the adviser will not assign the contract without the client's consent
that the adviser will obtain the client's consent before any change in the minority partners of the firm
that the adviser will not be compensated based on capital gains or appreciation, except as permitted
that, if the adviser is a partnership, it will notify the client of any change in the partnership's membership
questions.explanation: The USA requires three provisions: no performance fee except as permitted, no assignment without client consent, and, for a partnership, notice of membership changes. A change in a minority of partners requires only notification, not client consent, because it is not an assignment.

questions.q: ABC Advisers, a partnership with six partners, announces that a junior partner holding a 5% interest is retiring. Which statement is TRUE?
choices: All advisory contracts terminate automatically and must be re-signed
The change is an assignment of every advisory contract and requires each client's written consent
ABC must notify its advisory clients of the change within a reasonable time, but client consent is not required
ABC need take no action because the partner held only a minority interest
questions.explanation: A change in a minority of partners is not an assignment, so client consent is not required. The USA still requires a partnership adviser to notify clients of changes in its membership within a reasonable time. Doing nothing would violate that notice requirement, and consent would be needed only for a change of control.

questions.q:
Under NASAA's statement of policy on unethical business practices, a written investment advisory contract must disclose which of the following?
I. The services to be provided
II. The term of the contract
III. The advisory fee and the formula for computing it
IV. Whether the contract grants discretionary power to the adviser
choices: I and II only
I, II and III only
I, II, III and IV
II, III and IV only
questions.explanation: NASAA considers it unethical to enter into, extend or renew an advisory contract that is not in writing and does not disclose the services, the term, the fee and its formula, the amount of prepaid fees returned on termination, whether discretion is granted, and that the contract cannot be assigned without client consent. All four items are required.

questions.q: A new advisory contract contains this clause: "The Adviser shall not be liable for any losses in the Account, and Client waives all rights to bring claims under state or federal securities laws." Which statement is correct?
choices: The clause is acceptable if the client initials it separately
The clause is acceptable if the client is an accredited investor
The clause is acceptable if it is also disclosed in Form ADV Part 2A
The clause is a prohibited hedge clause; clients cannot waive their rights under the securities laws
questions.explanation: A hedge clause that tries to waive the client's rights under securities laws is prohibited. Under the USA, any condition binding a person to waive compliance with the Act is void. Initials, the client's wealth and disclosure elsewhere cannot make a non-waivable right waivable.

questions.q: Under the NASAA model brochure rule, a state-registered investment adviser must deliver its Form ADV Part 2 brochure to a prospective client:
choices: at least 10 business days before entering into the advisory contract
only if the prospective client requests it in writing
within 5 business days after the advisory contract is signed
at least 48 hours before entering into the advisory contract, or at the time of entering into it if the client may terminate without penalty within 5 business days
questions.explanation: NASAA's rule is 48 hours before signing, or at signing if the client has a 5-business-day penalty-free right to cancel. Delivery after signing does not meet the rule unless the cancellation right exists, and the brochure must be delivered whether or not the client asks for it.

questions.q: An investment adviser's books and records, including written communications relating to recommendations, generally must be kept for:
choices: 3 years, the first 2 years in an easily accessible place
5 years from the end of the fiscal year of the last entry, the first 2 years in an appropriate office of the adviser
7 years, all of it in the adviser's principal office
6 years from the date the account is closed
questions.explanation: Advisers Act Rule 204-2, and NASAA's parallel rule, require most IA records to be kept for 5 years from the end of the fiscal year of the last entry, with the first 2 years in an appropriate office of the adviser. The 3-year period is the broker-dealer rule for many communications, not the adviser rule.

questions.q: An IAR completed a two-day online course from an unaccredited organization and now uses the title "Certified Senior Retirement Specialist" on her business cards and website. Under NASAA's model rule, this is:
choices: an issue only if she uses the title in a written advertisement
permissible if she has at least 10 years of industry experience
an unethical practice, because the title misleadingly implies special training or expertise in advising seniors
permissible, because she did complete a course
questions.explanation: NASAA's model rule on senior-specific certifications treats using a senior designation that implies special training the person lacks, or that comes from an organization that is not properly accredited, as misleading. Completing a short course does not cure the problem, and the rule covers business cards and oral use, not just formal advertising.

questions.q: Under the SEC Marketing Rule, an SEC-registered investment adviser may include a client testimonial in an advertisement:
choices: if the ad clearly and prominently discloses that the person is a current client, whether compensation was provided, and any material conflicts of interest
only if the client is an accredited investor
under no circumstances, because testimonials are prohibited
only after the SEC pre-approves the advertisement
questions.explanation: The Marketing Rule, with a compliance date of November 2022, allows testimonials and endorsements when the required disclosures are made clearly and prominently and the adviser oversees compliance. The blanket ban was the old rule. The SEC does not pre-approve advertisements, and the client does not need to be accredited.

questions.q: An SEC-registered adviser's advertisement shows that its large-cap composite returned 12% gross of fees last year. Under the Marketing Rule, the ad must also:
choices: include written consent from every client in the composite
show net-of-fee performance with at least equal prominence, calculated over the same period and using the same methodology
state that the SEC has reviewed the performance calculation
show performance only since the composite's inception
questions.explanation: Gross performance may appear only alongside net performance of at least equal prominence, calculated over the same period with the same method. An ad may never say or imply that the SEC reviewed or approved the performance. The rule requires 1-, 5- and 10-year periods, not since-inception only.

questions.q: An adviser manages 10 portfolios with substantially similar objectives and strategies. Its new advertisement shows only the three best-performing portfolios. Under the SEC Marketing Rule, this is:
choices: prohibited unless the advertised results are not materially higher than they would be if all related portfolios were included
permissible if the ad discloses that 3 of 10 portfolios are shown
permissible because an adviser may select any subset of accounts to advertise
permissible if the results are presented net of fees
questions.explanation: The related-performance provision is aimed at cherry-picking. An ad must include all related portfolios, and may leave some out only if doing so does not produce materially higher results. Disclosing the omission or showing net figures does not fix a misleading selection.

questions.q: A client posts a glowing comment about her adviser on a public social media site. The firm reposts it on its own business page with the comment "Thank you. We couldn't agree more!" Which statement is correct?
choices: The repost is a problem only if more than 25 people view it
By endorsing and sharing the post, the firm has adopted it, so it is treated as the firm's own communication subject to advertising rules
Content created by third parties can never be attributed to the firm
The repost is a problem only if the client was paid
questions.explanation: When a firm explicitly or implicitly endorses third-party content, for example by sharing it with an approving comment, it adopts the content and becomes responsible for it as its own. Here it becomes a testimonial with the disclosures that requires. Payment affects which disclosures are needed, not whether the content is attributed to the firm, and the 25-person count is a FINRA category test, not an adoption test.

questions.q:
Which of the following would violate the general prohibitions of the SEC Marketing Rule?
I. Discussing an investment's potential benefits without fair and balanced treatment of its material risks
II. Including a material statement of fact the adviser has no reasonable basis to believe it can substantiate
III. Presenting net-of-fee performance alongside gross performance
IV. Stating that the firm is registered with the SEC
choices: II and IV
I and II
III and IV
I and III
questions.explanation: Items I and II are two of the rule's seven general prohibitions. Showing net performance alongside gross is required, not prohibited. Stating the fact of SEC registration is permitted, as long as the ad does not imply that registration means approval or a particular level of skill.

questions.q: An agent of a broker-dealer takes part in a real-time interactive discussion on a social media site about the securities markets. Under FINRA guidance, these interactive posts generally:
choices: must be filed with FINRA 10 business days before use
are treated like correspondence: supervised and retained, but not subject to principal pre-approval
are exempt from recordkeeping because they are informal
must be approved by a principal before each post
questions.explanation: FINRA separates static content (profiles, banner ads), which is a retail communication requiring principal pre-approval, from interactive content, which is supervised like correspondence without pre-approval. Business communications on social media must always be retained.

questions.q: Under the SEC Marketing Rule, hypothetical performance, such as backtested model results, may be included in an advertisement only if:
choices: it is labeled "hypothetical" anywhere in the advertisement
the adviser has policies and procedures reasonably designed to ensure it is relevant to the likely financial situation and objectives of the intended audience, and discloses its assumptions and risks
the backtest covers at least 10 years of data
it is shown to a mass retail audience through general media
questions.explanation: Hypothetical performance is permitted only with policies and procedures ensuring it is relevant to the intended audience, plus sufficient information about the criteria, assumptions and risks. In practice this limits it to audiences with the resources to analyze it, the opposite of mass retail distribution. A label alone, or a long backtest period, does not meet the conditions.

questions.q: Maria signs a performance-fee advisory contract in August 2026 and will have $1.2 million under management with the adviser. Her net worth is $3.1 million, which includes $500,000 of equity in her primary residence. Using the SEC qualified client thresholds effective June 29, 2026 ($1.4 million AUM or a net worth over $2.7 million), may the adviser charge her a performance-based fee?
choices: No, because her AUM is below $1.4 million and her net worth excluding her primary residence is only $2.6 million
Yes, because her AUM exceeds $1.1 million
Yes, as long as she consents in writing to the fee
Yes, because her total net worth exceeds $2.7 million
questions.explanation: A qualified client needs at least $1.4 million under management with the adviser, or a net worth over $2.7 million excluding the primary residence. $3.1 million − $0.5 million = $2.6 million, and her AUM is $1.2 million, so she meets neither test. $1.1 million was the old AUM threshold, which applies only to contracts grandfathered from before June 29, 2026. Counting the home in net worth is not allowed, and written consent cannot substitute for qualified-client status.

questions.q:
Under the Section 28(e) safe harbor, which of the following may an investment adviser obtain with client soft dollars?
I. Research reports on specific companies and industries
II. Analytical software used in making investment decisions
III. Rent for the adviser's office
IV. Airfare and hotel costs to attend a research conference
choices: I and III
II and IV
I and II
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation: Section 28(e) protects paying for brokerage and research services that help with investment decisions, such as research reports and analytical software. Overhead such as rent, and travel and lodging, even for a research conference, fall outside the safe harbor. The conference fee for research content could qualify, but the travel costs cannot.

questions.q: An investment adviser wants to sell a corporate bond from its own inventory to an advisory client. Under the Investment Advisers Act and NASAA rules, the adviser must:
choices: disclose its capacity on the trade confirmation after settlement
disclose in writing the capacity in which it is acting and obtain the client's consent before completion of the transaction
obtain blanket written consent at account opening covering all future principal trades
do nothing further as long as the price is fair
questions.explanation: Section 206(3) requires, for each principal transaction, written disclosure of the adviser's capacity and the client's consent before completion. Blanket advance consent is not enough for principal trades; it is allowed only for agency cross transactions. Disclosure after the trade is too late, and a fair price does not remove the disclosure and consent requirement.

questions.q: Which statement about agency cross transactions by an investment adviser is TRUE?
choices: The adviser may effect an agency cross when it recommended the transaction to both the buyer and the seller
The client's oral consent must be obtained before each transaction
No trade confirmation is required if the client gave written consent
The client may give prospective written consent, which it may revoke at any time
questions.explanation: Rule 206(3)-2 permits agency cross transactions with the client's prospective (blanket) written consent after full disclosure. The adviser must send confirmations and an annual summary, and must tell the client the consent is revocable at any time. It is prohibited when the adviser recommended the trade to both sides.

questions.q: For which client would a wrap fee account most likely be UNSUITABLE?
choices: A client who wants predictable, bundled costs for advice and execution
A client who uses several money managers in a single program
An active investor who rebalances monthly and wants professional management
A retiree who holds a few blue-chip stocks and Treasury bonds and trades once or twice a year
questions.explanation: A wrap fee bundles advisory, execution and custody costs into one asset-based fee. A buy-and-hold investor who rarely trades would usually pay less with commissions plus a separate fee, so putting that client in a wrap account ('reverse churning') may be unsuitable. Active traders and clients who want predictable costs are the typical wrap candidates.

questions.q: An investment adviser's client is NOT a qualified client. Each of the following compensation arrangements would be permissible EXCEPT:
choices: an annual fee of 1% of the account's average quarterly asset value
an hourly fee of $250 for preparing a financial plan
a fee equal to 20% of the account's net capital gains for the year
a flat annual fee of $3,000
questions.explanation: A fee based on a share of capital gains or appreciation is a performance fee and is allowed only for qualified clients. A fee based on average asset value over a period is not a performance fee, even though it grows with the account, and flat or hourly fees are always permitted if reasonable and disclosed.

questions.q: Which statement about soft-dollar arrangements is TRUE?
choices: Research obtained with soft dollars may benefit only the specific account whose commissions paid for it
Soft dollars may pay for office furniture as long as the arrangement is disclosed
To use the safe harbor, the adviser must always obtain the lowest commission available

An adviser may pay more than the lowest available commission if it determines in good faith that the commission is reasonable relative to the value of the brokerage and research received, and it must disclose the arrangement
questions.explanation: Section 28(e) protects paying higher commissions in good faith for eligible brokerage and research, and the arrangement must be disclosed in Form ADV. Research does not have to benefit only the account that generated the commissions. Furniture is overhead no matter what is disclosed, and the whole point of the safe harbor is that the lowest commission is not required.

questions.q: An adviser regularly places clients in a mutual fund's Class A shares, which pay 12b-1 fees to the adviser's affiliated broker-dealer, even though a lower-cost institutional share class of the same fund is available to these clients. The adviser never disclosed the conflict. Which statement is correct?
choices: There is no violation because 12b-1 fees are disclosed in the fund's prospectus
The adviser breached its fiduciary duty by failing to disclose the conflict and failing to act in the clients' best interest on cost
The practice is acceptable because 12b-1 fees are capped at 1% per year
There is a violation only if a client files a written complaint
questions.explanation: Choosing a higher-cost share class that benefits the adviser, without disclosing the conflict, violates the duties of loyalty and care. The SEC's share class initiative sanctioned many advisers for exactly this. Prospectus disclosure by the fund does not satisfy the adviser's own disclosure duty, and a violation does not depend on a client complaint.

questions.q:
Which of the following would give an investment adviser custody of client assets?
I. Authority to deduct advisory fees directly from client accounts
II. Serving as trustee of a client's family trust
III. A general power of attorney allowing withdrawals from the client's account
IV. A limited trading authorization to buy and sell securities in the client's account
choices: I and IV
II and III only
I, II and III
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation: Custody includes any authority to obtain client funds or securities: fee deduction, a general power of attorney allowing withdrawals, and legal roles such as trustee. A limited trading authorization allows trading but not withdrawals, so it is discretion, not custody.

questions.q: A client mails a stock certificate directly to her investment adviser's office by mistake. To avoid having custody, the adviser should return the certificate to the sender within:
choices: 30 calendar days
10 business days
5 business days
3 business days
questions.explanation: Under the custody rules, inadvertently receiving client funds or securities is not custody if the adviser returns them to the sender promptly, and in any case within 3 business days.

questions.q: An investment adviser has custody of client assets for reasons other than deducting its fees. In general, the adviser must:
choices: have client funds and securities verified by an independent certified public accountant through a surprise examination at least once each calendar year
submit to a surprise audit by the Administrator's staff once each calendar year
have client funds and securities verified by an independent CPA through a scheduled examination each quarter
have the assets examined only when a client requests it
questions.explanation: The custody rule requires an annual surprise examination by an independent CPA, at a time chosen by the accountant without prior notice. It is not quarterly, it is not performed by the Administrator's staff, and it does not depend on a client request.

questions.q: Under the NASAA model custody rule, an investment adviser with custody must have a reasonable basis for believing that the qualified custodian sends each client an account statement at least:
choices: quarterly
semiannually
annually
monthly
questions.explanation: The adviser must have a reasonable basis, after due inquiry, for believing the qualified custodian sends statements at least quarterly. The statement shows the funds and securities held at the end of the period and all transactions during it.

questions.q: A state-registered investment adviser with custody of client funds must meet each of the following requirements EXCEPT:
choices: notify the Administrator on Form ADV that it has or may have custody
maintain client funds and securities with a qualified custodian
notify clients in writing of the qualified custodian's name and address and how the assets are held
obtain the Administrator's prior written approval before accepting custody of any client account
questions.explanation: Under the NASAA model rule the adviser must notify the Administrator promptly on Form ADV, use a qualified custodian and tell clients where their assets are held. There is no requirement to obtain the Administrator's prior approval for each account.

questions.q: An investment adviser's only form of custody is that it deducts its advisory fees directly from client accounts. Under the NASAA model rule, the adviser must:
choices: have the client's written authorization, and each time send the custodian a notice of the fee and the client an itemized invoice showing how the fee was calculated
have an independent CPA verify each fee deduction before it is processed
obtain the Administrator's approval before each fee deduction
deduct fees no more than once per calendar year
questions.explanation: The fee-deduction safeguards are written client authorization, written notice of the fee to the qualified custodian, and an itemized invoice to the client (fee, formula, period and asset value). There is no requirement for regulatory approval or CPA verification of each deduction, and fees may be deducted as often as the contract provides, typically quarterly.

questions.q: An investment adviser is the general partner of a limited partnership whose limited partners are advisory clients. Instead of having quarterly statements sent to each investor, the adviser may satisfy the custody rule by distributing audited financial statements to all investors within how many days after the end of the fund's fiscal year?
choices: 180 days
90 days
45 days
120 days
questions.explanation: Acting as general partner of a pooled vehicle gives the adviser custody. Under the SEC and NASAA custody rules, the adviser can replace quarterly statements by having the fund audited annually and delivering the audited financial statements, prepared under GAAP, to investors within 120 days of fiscal year-end.

questions.q: An IAR receives oral discretionary authority from a new advisory client and places the first discretionary trade today. Under NASAA's statement of policy, the IAR must obtain written discretionary authority:
choices: within 30 calendar days after the account is opened
before placing the first discretionary transaction
within 10 business days after the date of the first discretionary transaction
never, because investment advisers do not need written discretionary authority
questions.explanation: NASAA's IA policy allows an adviser to act on oral discretion at first but requires written authorization within 10 business days after the first discretionary transaction. Getting written authority before the first trade is the broker-dealer agent standard, not the adviser standard.

questions.q: A client tells her agent, "Buy 500 shares of XYZ for me today. Use your judgment on the timing and price." Which statement is correct?
choices: The agent may choose to buy a different security if XYZ becomes too expensive
The order stays in effect until it is filled, however long that takes
This is time-and-price discretion, which does not require written discretionary authority, and the order expires at the end of the business day unless the client authorizes otherwise in writing
This is full discretion, so the agent must have written discretionary authority before entering the order
questions.explanation: The client chose the asset, the action and the amount, so only time and price are left to the agent, which is not discretion. Under FINRA 3260, time-and-price discretion lasts only for the business day it is granted unless the client gives written authorization otherwise. Buying a different security would require true discretion the agent does not have.

questions.q:
Which of the following decisions would require discretionary authority if made without first consulting the client?
I. Selecting the security to be bought
II. Deciding the number of shares
III. Choosing the time of execution during the day
IV. Deciding whether to buy or to sell
choices: I, II and IV
I and II only
III and IV
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation: Discretion means deciding the asset (I), the amount (II) or the action (IV). Choosing only the time, or price, of execution is not discretion.

questions.q: An agent of a broker-dealer receives oral discretionary authority from a customer on Monday, makes a discretionary purchase on Tuesday, and receives the signed written discretionary authorization on Thursday. Which statement is correct?
choices: The agent committed an unethical practice, because an agent must have written discretionary authority before exercising discretion
There is a violation only if the Tuesday trade lost money
There is no violation, because the customer gave oral authority first
There is no violation, because written authority was received within 10 business days
questions.explanation: NASAA's broker-dealer and agent policy makes exercising discretion without prior written authorization an unethical practice. The 10-business-day grace period applies only to investment advisers and IARs. The outcome of the trade is irrelevant.

questions.q: An agent notices that a stock is rallying and buys 200 shares for a customer's non-discretionary account without contacting the customer. The stock rises 15% the next day. The agent's action is:
choices: unethical only if the stock was unsuitable for the customer
unethical, because it is an unauthorized trade regardless of the profit
acceptable, because the customer benefited
acceptable if the customer approves it after the fact
questions.explanation: In a non-discretionary account every trade needs the customer's prior approval. Trading without it is unauthorized trading, an unethical practice whatever the result. Approval after the fact does not cure the violation.

questions.q: Which statement about discretionary advisory accounts is TRUE?
choices: Discretionary authority allows the adviser to disregard the client's stated investment objectives
Discretionary authority allows the adviser to withdraw funds from the account to pay third parties
Even with discretionary authority, an adviser may not make transactions that are excessive in size or frequency given the client's resources and the character of the account
Once granted, discretionary authority cannot be revoked by the client for one year
questions.explanation: Discretion never overrides suitability or the client's objectives. Excessive trading in a discretionary account is an unethical practice (churning). Withdrawal authority is custody, not discretion, and the client may revoke discretion at any time.

questions.q:
An IAR needs a $20,000 short-term loan. From which of the following advisory clients may the IAR borrow the money?
I. A commercial bank that is an advisory client and routinely makes personal loans
II. A client who is also the IAR's close friend
III. A wealthy retired client who offers a below-market interest rate
IV. An elderly client who insists on helping
choices: I and II
I, II and III
I, II, III and IV
I only
questions.explanation: NASAA treats borrowing from a client as unethical unless the client is a financial institution in the business of lending money (the IA policy also permits a broker-dealer or affiliate client). Friendship, favorable terms or the client's insistence do not create an exception, and borrowing from an elderly client raises exploitation concerns too.

questions.q: An agent wants to open a joint account with a customer and share in its profits and losses. This is permissible only if:
choices: the customer gives written consent; broker-dealer approval is not needed
the customer gives oral consent and the account is profitable
the agent contributes at least 50% of the money in the account
the agent has written authorization from both the customer and the broker-dealer, and shares in proportion to the agent's own financial contribution
questions.explanation: Sharing in a customer account requires written authorization from both the customer and the employing broker-dealer, and the agent's share must be in direct proportion to the agent's contribution (accounts of immediate family are an exception). The customer's written consent alone is not enough, and there is no minimum contribution requirement.

questions.q: Without telling his broker-dealer, an agent sells shares of a friend's private real estate venture to several of his customers and receives a fee from the issuer. This practice is known as:
choices: front running
churning
selling away
scalping
questions.explanation: Effecting securities transactions that are not recorded on the broker-dealer's books, without the firm's prior written authorization, is selling away, an unethical practice under NASAA's policy. Front running is trading ahead of customer orders, churning is excessive trading, and scalping is buying ahead of your own recommendation.

questions.q: A trader at a broker-dealer learns that an institutional customer is about to place an order to buy 500,000 shares of a thinly traded stock. Before entering the customer's order, the trader buys 5,000 shares for his personal account. This is an example of:
choices: scalping
selling away
a principal transaction
front running
questions.explanation: Trading for your own account ahead of a customer's block order you know about, to profit from the price move it will cause, is front running. Scalping is the adviser's version of trading around its own recommendations, not around customer orders.

questions.q: Regarding insider trading, each of the following statements is true EXCEPT:
choices: the SEC may seek a civil penalty of up to three times the profit gained or loss avoided
a firm that fails to take appropriate steps to prevent insider trading by its employees may face civil penalties as a controlling person
a tipper who passes material nonpublic information to a friend cannot be liable unless the tipper also trades
investment advisers must establish, maintain and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to prevent the misuse of material nonpublic information
questions.explanation: Both tippers and tippees are liable. A tipper who passes material nonpublic information in breach of a duty violates the law even without trading. The other statements are accurate: Section 204A requires written MNPI procedures, and ITSFEA provides for civil penalties of up to three times the profit gained or loss avoided, along with controlling-person liability.

questions.q:
Which of the following actions by an agent would be considered unethical?
I. Telling a customer, "If this stock goes down, I'll personally make up the difference"
II. Describing a U.S. Treasury bond as backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. government
III. Making excessive trades in a customer's account to generate commissions
IV. Describing an insured municipal bond as being insured as to timely payment of principal and interest
choices: I and II
I and III
II and IV
I, III and IV
questions.explanation: Guaranteeing a customer against loss (I) and churning (III) are unethical. Accurately describing a third party's guarantee or insurance on a security (II and IV) is a factual description, not a promise by the agent.

questions.q: Under the SEC's code of ethics rule for investment advisers, access persons must obtain the firm's pre-approval before acquiring:
choices: securities in an initial public offering or a limited offering (private placement)
shares of any open-end mutual fund
U.S. Treasury securities
any security worth more than $10,000
questions.explanation: Rule 204A-1 requires pre-approval for access persons' purchases of IPOs and limited offerings, where conflicts and allocation abuses are most likely. Access persons also file holdings reports (within 10 days and annually) and quarterly transaction reports. Treasuries and most open-end fund shares are not reportable securities, and there is no general dollar-size pre-approval rule.

questions.q: An investment adviser buys 10,000 shares of a small-cap stock for its own account, then publishes a newsletter strongly recommending the stock, and sells its shares after subscribers' buying drives the price up. This practice is called:
choices: scalping
an agency cross transaction
front running
selling away
questions.explanation: Scalping is buying a security, recommending it without disclosing your intent to sell, and then selling into the price rise the recommendation causes. It is a fraudulent practice under Advisers Act Section 206. Front running involves trading ahead of customer orders, not your own recommendation.

questions.q: Which of the following is part of an investment adviser's duty of LOYALTY rather than its duty of care?
choices: Making a reasonable inquiry into the client's financial situation and objectives
Making full and fair disclosure of all material facts about the relationship, including conflicts of interest
Monitoring the client's account at a frequency consistent with the agreed relationship
Seeking best execution for client transactions
questions.explanation: Under the SEC's 2019 interpretation, the duty of loyalty requires the adviser not to put its own interests first and to make full and fair disclosure of material facts and conflicts. Best execution, monitoring and understanding the client (best-interest advice) are all parts of the duty of care.

questions.q: Regulation Best Interest requires a broker-dealer that makes a recommendation to a retail customer to:
choices: apply the standard only to institutional customers
act as a fiduciary in all dealings with the customer
monitor the customer's account on an ongoing basis after every recommendation
act in the retail customer's best interest at the time the recommendation is made, without placing the firm's interests ahead of the customer's
questions.explanation: Reg BI sets a best-interest standard at the time of the recommendation, through its disclosure, care, conflict-of-interest and compliance obligations. It is not a fiduciary standard. It does not generally require ongoing monitoring unless the firm agrees to monitor, and it protects retail customers, not institutions.

questions.q: Under NASAA's statement of policy on unethical practices of investment advisers, each of the following is unethical EXCEPT:
choices: basing advice on a published research report without naming the report's author to the client
giving a client a custom report prepared by another firm without disclosing that fact
charging a client an unreasonable advisory fee
disclosing a client's identity and holdings to a third party without consent when not required by law
questions.explanation: NASAA considers it unethical to provide a report or recommendation prepared by someone else without disclosing that fact, but the policy expressly excludes using published research reports or statistical analyses to render advice. Unauthorized disclosure of client information and unreasonable fees are both on the list.

questions.q: Which statement about Form CRS (the client relationship summary) is TRUE?
choices: It is limited to 2 pages (4 for dual registrants), and an investment adviser must deliver it to a retail investor before or at the time of entering into an advisory contract
It is delivered only if the client requests it in writing
It must be approved by the state Administrator before it is given to clients
It is delivered only to institutional clients
questions.explanation: Form CRS is a short plain-English summary for retail investors: at most 2 pages, or 4 for a dual registrant. Advisers deliver it before or at the time of the advisory contract. It is filed with regulators but not 'approved' by them, and delivery is required, not on request.

questions.q: An investment adviser with discretion over brokerage has a duty to seek best execution. Best execution is BEST described as:
choices: always using the broker-dealer that charges the lowest commission
executing every order within one minute of receipt
routing all trades to the broker-dealer affiliated with the adviser
seeking the most favorable terms reasonably available, considering price, commission, speed, reliability and the value of research and services
questions.explanation: Best execution looks at the overall quality of the execution, not only the commission rate. That is why Section 28(e) lets an adviser pay a higher commission in good faith for valuable research. Automatically routing to an affiliate raises a conflict and is not the definition of best execution.

questions.q:
Under NASAA's statement of policy on dishonest or unethical practices of broker-dealers and agents, which of the following are unethical?
I. Failing to bring a customer's written complaint to the broker-dealer's attention
II. Splitting a commission with another agent registered with the same broker-dealer
III. Recommending a security without reasonable grounds to believe it is suitable for the customer
IV. Entering orders near the close of trading to artificially influence a stock's closing price
choices: I, III and IV
II and IV
I and III only
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation: Failing to forward written complaints (I), unsuitable recommendations (III) and market manipulation such as marking the close (IV) are unethical. Splitting commissions is prohibited only with persons who are not registered agents of the same or an affiliated broker-dealer, so sharing with a registered colleague at the same firm (II) is permitted.

questions.q: On one business day, a customer delivers $6,000 in currency to a broker-dealer in the morning and another $5,000 in currency that afternoon. Which statement is correct?
choices: No report is required, because neither deposit exceeded $10,000
The firm must file a Currency Transaction Report, because cash transactions in one business day totaling more than $10,000 are aggregated
The firm must file a Suspicious Activity Report instead of a CTR
The firm must reject both deposits
questions.explanation: CTR rules add together multiple currency transactions by or for the same person in one business day. $6,000 + $5,000 = $11,000, which is more than $10,000, so a CTR is required. A CTR is routine and does not by itself mean a SAR is needed, although a SAR may also be filed if the activity is suspicious.

questions.q: Which statement about Suspicious Activity Reports filed by broker-dealers is TRUE?
choices: A SAR is required only when the firm has proof that a crime was committed
The firm must notify the customer within 30 days after filing a SAR
A SAR is required only for cash transactions of more than $10,000
A SAR is required for suspicious transactions involving $5,000 or more, and the firm may not tell the customer that a SAR was filed
questions.explanation: Broker-dealers must file SARs for transactions of $5,000 or more that they know, suspect or have reason to suspect are suspicious, generally within 30 days of detection. Proof is not required. 'Tipping off' the customer is prohibited. The over-$10,000 cash threshold belongs to the CTR.

questions.q: A customer tells her agent that she wants to deposit $9,500 in cash on each of the next four days "so I don't have to deal with the government paperwork." Which statement is correct?
choices: This is permitted if the customer can document that the money came from a legitimate source
This is permitted, because each deposit is under the $10,000 CTR threshold
The agent should advise the customer to reduce each deposit to under $5,000
This is structuring, which is a federal crime even if the funds are legitimate, and the firm should consider filing a SAR
questions.explanation: Deliberately breaking up cash deposits to avoid a CTR is structuring, a crime regardless of where the money came from, and it is a classic red flag for a SAR. An agent who suggests other amounts to avoid reporting would be helping to structure.

questions.q: A customer wires funds through a series of accounts at banks in three different countries and then buys and quickly sells securities, all to obscure where the money came from. This is the money-laundering stage known as:
choices: structuring
layering
placement
integration
questions.explanation: Layering hides the source of funds through a series of transactions. Placement is getting illegal cash into the financial system, and integration is returning the cleaned money to the legitimate economy. Structuring is a method of avoiding cash reports, not one of the three stages.

questions.q:
Under the Customer Identification Program rules, a broker-dealer must obtain which of the following from an individual before opening an account?
I. Name
II. Date of birth
III. Residential or business street address
IV. An identification number, such as a Social Security number for a U.S. person
choices: I and IV only
I, II, III and IV
I, III and IV only
II, III and IV only
questions.explanation: The CIP minimum for an individual is name, date of birth, address (a street address, not only a P.O. box) and an identification number (a TIN for U.S. persons; a passport or other government ID number for non-U.S. persons). All four are required.

questions.q: A broker-dealer's screening shows that the beneficiary of an outgoing wire requested by a customer appears on OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals list, and the match is confirmed. The firm should:
choices: block (freeze) the funds and report to OFAC within 10 business days
process the wire and then file a Suspicious Activity Report
return the funds to the customer and close the account
file a Currency Transaction Report
questions.explanation: When a transaction involves an SDN, the firm must block or reject it as the sanctions program requires and report to OFAC within 10 business days. Processing the wire would violate sanctions, returning the funds would defeat the block, and a CTR concerns cash, not sanctions.

questions.q: Under Regulation S-P, a broker-dealer must deliver a privacy notice to a customer:
choices: only if the firm shares information with affiliates
only when the customer relationship is established
when the customer relationship is established and annually after that, unless the firm qualifies for the annual-notice exception
only when the customer requests one in writing
questions.explanation: An initial notice is required no later than the start of the customer relationship, and an annual notice is required while the relationship continues. The exception applies to firms that share information only under the statutory exceptions and have not changed their policies. An initial notice alone is not enough when the exception does not apply.

questions.q: Before an investment adviser subject to Regulation S-P shares a customer's nonpublic personal information with a nonaffiliated third-party marketing company, and no exception applies, federal rules require the adviser to:
choices: obtain the SEC's approval
do nothing further if the data is encrypted
give the customer an opt-out notice and a reasonable opportunity to opt out
obtain the customer's written opt-in consent
questions.explanation: Regulation S-P (under Gramm-Leach-Bliley) uses an opt-out model for sharing NPI with nonaffiliated third parties outside the exceptions: notice plus a reasonable chance to opt out. Opt-in is not the federal requirement, and encryption is not an exception to the notice requirement.

questions.q: Under the 2024 amendments to Regulation S-P, a covered firm that discovers unauthorized access to sensitive customer information must notify affected individuals:
choices: as soon as practicable, but no later than 30 days after becoming aware of the incident
only if the customer suffers a financial loss
within 72 hours after becoming aware of the incident
within 90 days after the end of the calendar quarter
questions.explanation: The 2024 amendments require an incident response program and notice to affected individuals within 30 days of becoming aware of an incident in which sensitive customer information was, or is reasonably likely to have been, accessed or used without authorization. The 72-hour deadline applies to service providers notifying the firm, not to customer notice.

questions.q:
NASAA's model rule on business continuity and succession planning requires a state-registered investment adviser's written plan to address which of the following?
I. Protection, backup and recovery of books and records
II. Alternate means of communicating with clients, key personnel, custodians and regulators
III. Office relocation if the principal place of business is lost
IV. Assignment of duties to qualified persons if key personnel die or become unavailable
choices: I, II, III and IV
II, III and IV only
I, II and III only
I and II only
questions.explanation: The NASAA model rule requires written procedures covering all four items, along with otherwise minimizing service disruption and client harm. The succession item (IV) is especially important for small and one-person advisers.

questions.q: An IAR in a state that has adopted NASAA's Model Act to Protect Vulnerable Adults reasonably believes that an 82-year-old client's new caregiver is behind a request to withdraw $50,000. Which statement is correct?
choices: The firm must first notify the caregiver and give the caregiver a chance to explain
The firm may freeze the account indefinitely until the client's family resolves the matter
The firm may delay the disbursement, which expires after 15 business days unless the Administrator or Adult Protective Services requests an extension of up to 10 more business days
The firm must process the disbursement because the client has authorized it
questions.explanation: The model act lets a firm delay a disbursement it reasonably believes involves financial exploitation. It must notify the account's authorized parties, other than a suspected exploiter, within 2 business days and report to the Administrator and APS. The delay lasts up to 15 business days, extendable by up to 10 more at the request of the Administrator or APS. Indefinite freezes are not allowed, and the suspected exploiter is not notified.

questions.q: Under FINRA Rule 4512, when a broker-dealer opens a new account for a non-institutional customer, it must:
choices: refuse to open the account unless the customer names a trusted contact person
require that the trusted contact person be an immediate family member
make reasonable efforts to obtain the name and contact information of a trusted contact person, but may open the account if the customer declines to provide one
give the trusted contact person limited trading authority over the account
questions.explanation: FINRA 4512 requires reasonable efforts to obtain a trusted contact (age 18 or older). A customer's refusal does not prevent the account from opening. The trusted contact has no trading authority; the firm may contact them about suspected exploitation, the customer's health or whereabouts, or a guardian or executor. They do not have to be a family member.
